goal_tracking.trigger_summary: At the fifth-watch dock, Liu Sanniang publicly slaps the waist token back into Lu Wenfeng's palm, snatches away the empty casket, and orders Ashun to push off with the pole and send him away by water; Lu Wenfeng accepts the token and boards the boat, responding to her line “I won't wait for you” with “no one waits for anyone else to throw their life away”, and adds, “there is a mechanism in the empty casket; it is fine if others open it, but you must not touch it”. Liu Sanniang's immediate tactical goal shifts from “keep the waist token clenched in her own hand, draw the pursuers toward her own line, and send Lu Wenfeng cleanly to the Earth God Temple to scout the way” to “return the credential to Lu Wenfeng, use the empty casket as bait to draw the pursuers toward her own line, open for business as usual to protect the shell, avoid alarming the Canal Gang's old members, and three days later go to the appointment at Wupeng Dock with the token”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Arrange the food and lodging accounts for the regulars properly, while renewing old ties through reminiscing and taking the opportunity to inquire about recent movements in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Use the empty case as bait to draw the pursuers toward his own line, and send Lu Wenfeng, token in hand, along the water route to the Earth God Temple to scout the way; at the same time, open the doors as usual and release the rumor that “at the fifth watch he had settled the bill and gone south” to protect the shell, while guarding against unfamiliar faces in the building and old members of the canal gang. Three days later, go to the appointment at Wupeng Dock by token.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greeting an old regular, arranging food and lodging, quoting and settling the bill, and catching up while asking about recent circumstances.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motivation: Liu Sanniang wants to find out who is digging into the old case at Qixia Ferry, why the waist token that should have sunk into the river has resurfaced, who among the people who escorted the Qinglu is still alive, whether the person in the north who calls himself Lao Wu is real or fake, which group has pursued them to town, and whether Lu Wenfeng’s return this time is related to this—but even more, she wants to personally grip the proof for attending the appointment in her own palm, and decide for herself how this game will proceed. But this is only an inference, not yet confirmed by independent evidence.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng states that "what I ran into wasn't a hard case, but some people digging up old accounts," and directly asks, "Has anyone recently been asking about the old survivors of the battle at Qixia Ferry?"—directly touching the old case Liu Sanniang has not mentioned to anyone for twelve years.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng pushed one layer further: he asked about "the person who escorted the Qinglu across the ferry back then," showed "the Canal Gang waist token that should have sunk into the river with the corpse," and asserted that "on the night at Qixia Ferry, perhaps someone did not die at all"—pushing the old case from "someone is asking around" to "someone did not die, and physical evidence has appeared."

In her early years, Liu Sanniang was a female escort guard for the Canal Gang. In the battle at Qixia Ferry, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an inside traitor; the back courtyard of the inn is an unmarked message relay point, and gathering rumors has always been part of her daily routine.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang received the physical evidence through action: her fingers dug into the wood seams of the counter, her fingernail nearly snapping; she gripped Lu Wenfeng’s wrist, slammed the bronze key to the Tianzi Room heavily into his palm, lowered her voice and ordered him to “go upstairs” and bolt the door, arranged a private talk at midnight, and directly pressed, “That waist token—do you have it on you?”—she proactively shifted the conversation into a locked room, breaking a twelve-year taboo.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng confirmed “it is here” and added, “the people watching it have also arrived in town”—also handing over the layer of risk that the pursuers have already reached the doorstep, expanding what Liu Sanniang needs to understand from “whose waist token it is” to “which route the pursuers come from, and whether they are already among this hall full of guests.”

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang for the first time verbally put “guarding against the old members of the grain-transport gang” on the table—“After Old Five died, there were plenty of money-grubbing ingrates in that gang; I’m more on guard against them than you are”—which was tantamount to drawing a line, in front of Lu Wenfeng, between her old fellow disciples and the old guest before her.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng used a countersign to turn the midnight appointment into an executable trust contract (“Knock three times, pause for one breath, then knock twice”; “If it isn’t that number, I won’t open the door”), then turned back to warn her, “Sanniang, you be careful too”—for the first time expressing concern for Liu Sanniang herself, expanding the risk from the layer of physical evidence to her personally.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng’s first words upon entering were “Don’t turn the lamp brighter,” after which he immediately showed his waist token and previewed that “the person in the north also left a message”—expanding the showdown from “whose waist token is it” to “who is that northern route, and what message did they leave,” while locking this conversation into a room lit by only one dim lamp.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang snatched the waist token over with one hand; the instant her fingertips touched the eagle-claw engraving, she recognized that it was Lao Wu’s token, the special black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Tiegutang”, and even remembered the chipped corner of the token (broken off back then when Lao Wu blocked a blade for her). She pressed him with “Speak!”, demanding “That damned ghost up north—what message exactly did he bring you”—for the first time, in front of physical evidence from the old case, she actively reveals her personal relationship with the deceased, pushing the interrogation toward that line from the north.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng relayed the exact words of the person from the north without missing a single character—“What sank with the blue heron was an empty account; the living account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Wharf”—and added that the person “was missing half of his right ear and called himself Old Fifth.” At the end, he asked in return, “Would outsiders know about this scar?”—turning the old case from “someone didn’t die” into “the setup back then was itself fake,” while giving a date and place, and at the same time passing the ball of identity verification to Liu Sanniang.

At the fifth-watch dock in this turn, Liu Sanniang publicly slaps the waist token back into Lu Wenfeng's palm, takes away the empty box, and orders Ah Shun to raise the pole and send him off by water route—she actively returns the credential for going to Wupengwu to the token holder, while taking on the task of drawing away the tail, spelling out the move with "Leave the empty box to me; it's enough for me to run the dog noses in town in circles."

What Lu Wenfeng provides are the original words and identity details, but he does not explain in whose hands he saw the waist token, whom he suspects, or which group was watching the token; this is insufficient to determine that he came on this trip specifically for the old case.

When she returned the token in public, she brushed it off with a low scolding of 'grown wings now, have you, and think your old mother meddles too much,' which might also just be an ordinary spat between old acquaintances, not necessarily a deliberate return of evidence.
alternatives: She is only casually asking after a regular customer’s recent situation out of an innkeeper’s duty and old friendship; as for “Qixia Ferry” and the “Qinglu,” she simply does not want to say much.
She is paying attention to general jianghu movements as part of the inn’s routine message relay, unrelated to the old Qixia Ferry case.

She returned the card and seized the box, but was only left unable to save face by his line, “Don’t make decisions for me”; she may not necessarily be trying to take the part of drawing out the tail onto herself.

plot_point: At the fifth watch, at the backyard dock: in front of everyone, Liu Sanniang slapped the black-iron waist token back into Lu Wenfeng’s palm, then seized the empty case from his hand and ordered the boatman Ashun to pole off and send him away by water.

The reason Liu Sanniang gives is: the token is a death warrant; if he carries it, the dog noses on both water and land routes can catch the scent and chase him. Leaving the empty box with her is enough to lead the dog noses in town round and round.

Liu Sanniang settles both the returning of the plaque and the harsh words with, "Old friendship is old friendship, but remember this: that plaque was my sworn brother's life back then. When it comes to settling this debt, I am more qualified than you. If you die halfway, no one will collect your corpse for you." She also sets the rule for meeting with, "At the Earth God Temple. If you're late, this old woman won't wait for you."

Lu Wenfeng puts away the waist token and steps onto the small boat, accepting her line “I won’t wait for you” with “Just what I wanted—no one waits for anyone to get killed,” and then adds, “There’s a mechanism in the empty box. It’s fine if others open it; you mustn’t touch it”—laying bare the workings of the empty box to her while warning her not to touch it.

The suspended layer of voucher ownership has landed—the token is back in Lu Wenfeng’s hand—and the step of drawing out the tail has been handed back to Liu Sanniang—the empty box is in her hand. But “why she took it without telling anyone last night,” “what to take to Wupeng Dock three days later,” and “how her line will draw out the tail” remain unresolved, with the new added layer that “the empty box has a mechanism; do not touch it.”

Lu Wenfeng: His account is clean: the token was retrieved into his sleeve last night, the pouch is empty now, and he demands it back—she returned it in public, consistent from beginning to end, with no self-contradiction. Lu Wenfeng: She returns the token, seizes the box, and commands the boat in public, yet he still proceeds at his own pace: listening, watching, leaving room in his words. Her return and seizure determine what he gives next—whether to board the boat and leave, or to ask one layer deeper.

goal_tracking.trigger_summary: At the fifth-watch dock, Liu Sanniang publicly slaps the waist token back into Lu Wenfeng's palm, snatches away the empty casket, and orders Ashun to push off with the pole and send him away by water; Lu Wenfeng accepts the token and boards the boat, responding to her line “I won't wait for you” with “no one waits for anyone else to throw their life away”, and adds, “there is a mechanism in the empty casket; it is fine if others open it, but you must not touch it”. Liu Sanniang's immediate tactical goal shifts from “keep the waist token clenched in her own hand, draw the pursuers toward her own line, and send Lu Wenfeng cleanly to the Earth God Temple to scout the way” to “return the credential to Lu Wenfeng, use the empty casket as bait to draw the pursuers toward her own line, open for business as usual to protect the shell, avoid alarming the Canal Gang's old members, and three days later go to the appointment at Wupeng Dock with the token”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Arrange the food and lodging accounts for the regulars properly, while renewing old ties through reminiscing and taking the opportunity to inquire about recent movements in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Use the empty case as bait to draw the pursuers toward his own line, and send Lu Wenfeng, token in hand, along the water route to the Earth God Temple to scout the way; at the same time, open the doors as usual and release the rumor that “at the fifth watch he had settled the bill and gone south” to protect the shell, while guarding against unfamiliar faces in the building and old members of the canal gang. Three days later, go to the appointment at Wupeng Dock by token.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greeting an old regular, arranging food and lodging, quoting and settling the bill, and catching up while asking about recent circumstances.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motivation: Liu Sanniang wants to find out who is digging into the old case at Qixia Ferry, why the waist token that should have sunk into the river has resurfaced, who among the people who escorted the Qinglu is still alive, whether the person in the north who calls himself Lao Wu is real or fake, which group has pursued them to town, and whether Lu Wenfeng’s return this time is related to this—but even more, she wants to personally grip the proof for attending the appointment in her own palm, and decide for herself how this game will proceed. But this is only an inference, not yet confirmed by independent evidence.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng states that "what I ran into wasn't a hard case, but some people digging up old accounts," and directly asks, "Has anyone recently been asking about the old survivors of the battle at Qixia Ferry?"—directly touching the old case Liu Sanniang has not mentioned to anyone for twelve years.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng pushed one layer further: he asked about "the person who escorted the Qinglu across the ferry back then," showed "the Canal Gang waist token that should have sunk into the river with the corpse," and asserted that "on the night at Qixia Ferry, perhaps someone did not die at all"—pushing the old case from "someone is asking around" to "someone did not die, and physical evidence has appeared."

In her early years, Liu Sanniang was a female escort guard for the Canal Gang. In the battle at Qixia Ferry, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an inside traitor; the back courtyard of the inn is an unmarked message relay point, and gathering rumors has always been part of her daily routine.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang received the physical evidence through action: her fingers dug into the wood seams of the counter, her fingernail nearly snapping; she gripped Lu Wenfeng’s wrist, slammed the bronze key to the Tianzi Room heavily into his palm, lowered her voice and ordered him to “go upstairs” and bolt the door, arranged a private talk at midnight, and directly pressed, “That waist token—do you have it on you?”—she proactively shifted the conversation into a locked room, breaking a twelve-year taboo.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng confirmed “it is here” and added, “the people watching it have also arrived in town”—also handing over the layer of risk that the pursuers have already reached the doorstep, expanding what Liu Sanniang needs to understand from “whose waist token it is” to “which route the pursuers come from, and whether they are already among this hall full of guests.”

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang for the first time verbally put “guarding against the old members of the grain-transport gang” on the table—“After Old Five died, there were plenty of money-grubbing ingrates in that gang; I’m more on guard against them than you are”—which was tantamount to drawing a line, in front of Lu Wenfeng, between her old fellow disciples and the old guest before her.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng used a countersign to turn the midnight appointment into an executable trust contract (“Knock three times, pause for one breath, then knock twice”; “If it isn’t that number, I won’t open the door”), then turned back to warn her, “Sanniang, you be careful too”—for the first time expressing concern for Liu Sanniang herself, expanding the risk from the layer of physical evidence to her personally.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng’s first words upon entering were “Don’t turn the lamp brighter,” after which he immediately showed his waist token and previewed that “the person in the north also left a message”—expanding the showdown from “whose waist token is it” to “who is that northern route, and what message did they leave,” while locking this conversation into a room lit by only one dim lamp.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang snatched the waist token over with one hand; the instant her fingertips touched the eagle-claw engraving, she recognized that it was Lao Wu’s token, the special black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Tiegutang”, and even remembered the chipped corner of the token (broken off back then when Lao Wu blocked a blade for her). She pressed him with “Speak!”, demanding “That damned ghost up north—what message exactly did he bring you”—for the first time, in front of physical evidence from the old case, she actively reveals her personal relationship with the deceased, pushing the interrogation toward that line from the north.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng relayed the exact words of the person from the north without missing a single character—“What sank with the blue heron was an empty account; the living account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Wharf”—and added that the person “was missing half of his right ear and called himself Old Fifth.” At the end, he asked in return, “Would outsiders know about this scar?”—turning the old case from “someone didn’t die” into “the setup back then was itself fake,” while giving a date and place, and at the same time passing the ball of identity verification to Liu Sanniang.

At the fifth-watch dock in this turn, Liu Sanniang publicly slaps the waist token back into Lu Wenfeng's palm, takes away the empty box, and orders Ah Shun to raise the pole and send him off by water route—she actively returns the credential for going to Wupengwu to the token holder, while taking on the task of drawing away the tail, spelling out the move with "Leave the empty box to me; it's enough for me to run the dog noses in town in circles."
counter_evidence: Liu Sanniang’s response at this moment still uses greetings about food and lodging as the surface, and has not yet shown any particular urgency regarding the old case in the main hall.

What Lu Wenfeng provides are the original words and identity details, but he does not explain in whose hands he saw the waist token, whom he suspects, or which group was watching the token; this is insufficient to determine that he came on this trip specifically for the old case.

When she returned the token in public, she brushed it off with a low scolding of 'grown wings now, have you, and think your old mother meddles too much,' which might also just be an ordinary spat between old acquaintances, not necessarily a deliberate return of evidence.
alternatives: She is only casually asking after a regular customer’s recent situation out of an innkeeper’s duty and old friendship; as for “Qixia Ferry” and the “Qinglu,” she simply does not want to say much.
She is paying attention to general jianghu movements as part of the inn’s routine message relay, unrelated to the old Qixia Ferry case.

She returned the card and seized the box, but was only left unable to save face by his line, “Don’t make decisions for me”; she may not necessarily be trying to take the part of drawing out the tail onto herself.

plot_point: At the fifth watch, at the backyard dock: in front of everyone, Liu Sanniang slapped the black-iron waist token back into Lu Wenfeng’s palm, then seized the empty case from his hand and ordered the boatman Ashun to pole off and send him away by water.

The reason Liu Sanniang gives is: the token is a death warrant; if he carries it, the dog noses on both water and land routes can catch the scent and chase him. Leaving the empty box with her is enough to lead the dog noses in town round and round.

Liu Sanniang settles both the returning of the plaque and the harsh words with, "Old friendship is old friendship, but remember this: that plaque was my sworn brother's life back then. When it comes to settling this debt, I am more qualified than you. If you die halfway, no one will collect your corpse for you." She also sets the rule for meeting with, "At the Earth God Temple. If you're late, this old woman won't wait for you."

Lu Wenfeng puts away the waist token and steps onto the small boat, accepting her line “I won’t wait for you” with “Just what I wanted—no one waits for anyone to get killed,” and then adds, “There’s a mechanism in the empty box. It’s fine if others open it; you mustn’t touch it”—laying bare the workings of the empty box to her while warning her not to touch it.

The suspended layer of voucher ownership has landed—the token is back in Lu Wenfeng’s hand—and the step of drawing out the tail has been handed back to Liu Sanniang—the empty box is in her hand. But “why she took it without telling anyone last night,” “what to take to Wupeng Dock three days later,” and “how her line will draw out the tail” remain unresolved, with the new added layer that “the empty box has a mechanism; do not touch it.”

goal_tracking.trigger_summary: At the fifth-watch dock, Liu Sanniang publicly slaps the waist token back into Lu Wenfeng's palm, snatches away the empty casket, and orders Ashun to push off with the pole and send him away by water; Lu Wenfeng accepts the token and boards the boat, responding to her line “I won't wait for you” with “no one waits for anyone else to throw their life away”, and adds, “there is a mechanism in the empty casket; it is fine if others open it, but you must not touch it”. Liu Sanniang's immediate tactical goal shifts from “keep the waist token clenched in her own hand, draw the pursuers toward her own line, and send Lu Wenfeng cleanly to the Earth God Temple to scout the way” to “return the credential to Lu Wenfeng, use the empty casket as bait to draw the pursuers toward her own line, open for business as usual to protect the shell, avoid alarming the Canal Gang's old members, and three days later go to the appointment at Wupeng Dock with the token”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Arrange the food and lodging accounts for the regulars properly, while renewing old ties through reminiscing and taking the opportunity to inquire about recent movements in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Use the empty case as bait to draw the pursuers toward his own line, and send Lu Wenfeng, token in hand, along the water route to the Earth God Temple to scout the way; at the same time, open the doors as usual and release the rumor that “at the fifth watch he had settled the bill and gone south” to protect the shell, while guarding against unfamiliar faces in the building and old members of the canal gang. Three days later, go to the appointment at Wupeng Dock by token.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greeting an old regular, arranging food and lodging, quoting and settling the bill, and catching up while asking about recent circumstances.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motivation: Liu Sanniang wants to find out who is digging into the old case at Qixia Ferry, why the waist token that should have sunk into the river has resurfaced, who among the people who escorted the Qinglu is still alive, whether the person in the north who calls himself Lao Wu is real or fake, which group has pursued them to town, and whether Lu Wenfeng’s return this time is related to this—but even more, she wants to personally grip the proof for attending the appointment in her own palm, and decide for herself how this game will proceed. But this is only an inference, not yet confirmed by independent evidence.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng states that "what I ran into wasn't a hard case, but some people digging up old accounts," and directly asks, "Has anyone recently been asking about the old survivors of the battle at Qixia Ferry?"—directly touching the old case Liu Sanniang has not mentioned to anyone for twelve years.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng pushed one layer further: he asked about "the person who escorted the Qinglu across the ferry back then," showed "the Canal Gang waist token that should have sunk into the river with the corpse," and asserted that "on the night at Qixia Ferry, perhaps someone did not die at all"—pushing the old case from "someone is asking around" to "someone did not die, and physical evidence has appeared."

In her early years, Liu Sanniang was a female escort guard for the Canal Gang. In the battle at Qixia Ferry, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an inside traitor; the back courtyard of the inn is an unmarked message relay point, and gathering rumors has always been part of her daily routine.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang received the physical evidence through action: her fingers dug into the wood seams of the counter, her fingernail nearly snapping; she gripped Lu Wenfeng’s wrist, slammed the bronze key to the Tianzi Room heavily into his palm, lowered her voice and ordered him to “go upstairs” and bolt the door, arranged a private talk at midnight, and directly pressed, “That waist token—do you have it on you?”—she proactively shifted the conversation into a locked room, breaking a twelve-year taboo.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng confirmed “it is here” and added, “the people watching it have also arrived in town”—also handing over the layer of risk that the pursuers have already reached the doorstep, expanding what Liu Sanniang needs to understand from “whose waist token it is” to “which route the pursuers come from, and whether they are already among this hall full of guests.”

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang for the first time verbally put “guarding against the old members of the grain-transport gang” on the table—“After Old Five died, there were plenty of money-grubbing ingrates in that gang; I’m more on guard against them than you are”—which was tantamount to drawing a line, in front of Lu Wenfeng, between her old fellow disciples and the old guest before her.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng used a countersign to turn the midnight appointment into an executable trust contract (“Knock three times, pause for one breath, then knock twice”; “If it isn’t that number, I won’t open the door”), then turned back to warn her, “Sanniang, you be careful too”—for the first time expressing concern for Liu Sanniang herself, expanding the risk from the layer of physical evidence to her personally.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng’s first words upon entering were “Don’t turn the lamp brighter,” after which he immediately showed his waist token and previewed that “the person in the north also left a message”—expanding the showdown from “whose waist token is it” to “who is that northern route, and what message did they leave,” while locking this conversation into a room lit by only one dim lamp.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang snatched the waist token over with one hand; the instant her fingertips touched the eagle-claw engraving, she recognized that it was Lao Wu’s token, the special black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Tiegutang”, and even remembered the chipped corner of the token (broken off back then when Lao Wu blocked a blade for her). She pressed him with “Speak!”, demanding “That damned ghost up north—what message exactly did he bring you”—for the first time, in front of physical evidence from the old case, she actively reveals her personal relationship with the deceased, pushing the interrogation toward that line from the north.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng relayed the exact words of the person from the north without missing a single character—“What sank with the blue heron was an empty account; the living account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Wharf”—and added that the person “was missing half of his right ear and called himself Old Fifth.” At the end, he asked in return, “Would outsiders know about this scar?”—turning the old case from “someone didn’t die” into “the setup back then was itself fake,” while giving a date and place, and at the same time passing the ball of identity verification to Liu Sanniang.

At the fifth-watch dock in this turn, Liu Sanniang publicly slaps the waist token back into Lu Wenfeng's palm, takes away the empty box, and orders Ah Shun to raise the pole and send him off by water route—she actively returns the credential for going to Wupengwu to the token holder, while taking on the task of drawing away the tail, spelling out the move with "Leave the empty box to me; it's enough for me to run the dog noses in town in circles."
counter_evidence: Liu Sanniang’s response at this moment still uses greetings about food and lodging as the surface, and has not yet shown any particular urgency regarding the old case in the main hall.

What Lu Wenfeng provides are the original words and identity details, but he does not explain in whose hands he saw the waist token, whom he suspects, or which group was watching the token; this is insufficient to determine that he came on this trip specifically for the old case.

When she returned the token in public, she brushed it off with a low scolding of 'grown wings now, have you, and think your old mother meddles too much,' which might also just be an ordinary spat between old acquaintances, not necessarily a deliberate return of evidence.
alternatives: She is only casually asking after a regular customer’s recent situation out of an innkeeper’s duty and old friendship; as for “Qixia Ferry” and the “Qinglu,” she simply does not want to say much.
She is paying attention to general jianghu movements as part of the inn’s routine message relay, unrelated to the old Qixia Ferry case.

She returned the card and seized the box, but was only left unable to save face by his line, “Don’t make decisions for me”; she may not necessarily be trying to take the part of drawing out the tail onto herself.

original.rationale: Liu Sanniang has protected this matter for twelve years, so the safest response is to pretend it is ordinary; Lu Wenfeng also understands propriety—if she cannot force it out, he will not force it into her hands.

paths.label: Degrade

"Don't show up together." I take the black thread. "You stay in the temple and watch the rear route. I'll go test the rope and leave a mark. If I'm not back in half an incense stick, don't enter the stockade; withdraw immediately."

With a swift motion, I shove that length of black thread into your hand, then grab your collar and yank it downward, my eyes fixed hard on you as I lower my voice: “Brat, now you’re arranging things for this old lady. Fine. Your lightness skill is good and your sword is fast; going to scout the road is indeed more suitable for you than for these old bones of mine. I’ll stay here, get up onto the temple roof, and watch the rear for you. If there is the slightest stir within half a li, I’ll imitate a night owl three times. The moment you hear it, withdraw immediately!”

“As for that bullshit about ‘half an incense stick,’ take it back. If you don’t return by the appointed time, this old lady absolutely will not flee for her life alone. Even if I have to stake this token, I’ll punch a hole through Wupengwu! Keep your eyes sharp. Go!”

I slung the rag over my shoulder and laughed heartily. “Haven’t seen you in more than half a year, and you haven’t changed one bit. The moment you open your mouth, you ask for that good spot by the river. Lucky for you, the last Heaven-numbered private room just opened up, and I’ve kept it for you. The room price is the same as always: two qian a night.”

My hand, just about to collect the silver, suddenly paused for an instant. My fingertips pressed against the cold silver ingot before I quietly swept the money into the wooden box beneath the counter.

I did not touch the lampstand. Holding my breath, I stepped forward and snatched the waist token from you. The instant my fingertips touched the uneven talon engraving on it, my heart clenched hard—this was Old Five’s token, the specially made black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Ironbone Hall” back then. The notch on the corner of the token was from when it chipped as he blocked a blade for me all those years ago.

I put away the smile, step forward, clutch the token tightly in my palm, and lower my voice. “This thing belonged to Old Five. Back then, I hung it on his waist with my own hands. Now it’s become a death warrant. If you carry it on you, every dog’s nose on the water routes and land routes will catch the scent and chase after you. Leave the token with me, and the tails will be led away by me.

With a sharp motion, I slapped the cold black-iron token heavily back into his palm, and with the same movement snatched the empty box from his hand. I gave a cold laugh. "Old friendship is old friendship, but you remember this: back then, this token was my sworn brother's life. When it comes to settling this account, I have more right than you do.
I look at you, the corner of my eye twitching slightly, and in the end I do not argue with you over priority at a time like this.

I let go and give your shoulder a rough slap, my voice low but carrying an unquestionable ferocity: “As for that bullshit about ‘half an incense stick,’ take it back. If you don’t return by the appointed time, this old lady absolutely will not flee for her life alone. Even if I have to stake this token, I’ll punch a hole through Wupengwu! Keep your eyes sharp. Go!”

plot_point: At the fifth watch, at the backyard dock: in front of everyone, Liu Sanniang slapped the black-iron waist token back into Lu Wenfeng’s palm, then seized the empty case from his hand and ordered the boatman Ashun to pole off and send him away by water.

The reason Liu Sanniang gives is: the token is a death warrant; if he carries it, the dog noses on both water and land routes can catch the scent and chase him. Leaving the empty box with her is enough to lead the dog noses in town round and round.

Liu Sanniang settles both the returning of the plaque and the harsh words with, "Old friendship is old friendship, but remember this: that plaque was my sworn brother's life back then. When it comes to settling this debt, I am more qualified than you. If you die halfway, no one will collect your corpse for you." She also sets the rule for meeting with, "At the Earth God Temple. If you're late, this old woman won't wait for you."

Lu Wenfeng puts away the waist token and steps onto the small boat, accepting her line “I won’t wait for you” with “Just what I wanted—no one waits for anyone to get killed,” and then adds, “There’s a mechanism in the empty box. It’s fine if others open it; you mustn’t touch it”—laying bare the workings of the empty box to her while warning her not to touch it.

The suspended layer of voucher ownership has landed—the token is back in Lu Wenfeng’s hand—and the step of drawing out the tail has been handed back to Liu Sanniang—the empty box is in her hand. But “why she took it without telling anyone last night,” “what to take to Wupeng Dock three days later,” and “how her line will draw out the tail” remain unresolved, with the new added layer that “the empty box has a mechanism; do not touch it.”
attention: Liu Sanniang: He said “don't decide for me”, and she heard it, and acknowledged it—the moment she slapped the token back into his palm was the moment she withdrew the hand that had “decided his movements for him”. But withdrawing her hand does not mean leaving the stage: she still believes he can make it there, believes that once he reaches the Earth God Temple he will wait for her; only this belief is now mixed with a new layer of weighing—going forward, which matters she can decide for him and which she cannot must be redrawn.

Liu Sanniang: As soon as the token leaves his hand, the account book in her heart immediately turns a page: can an empty box fool the dog noses on both the water and land routes? If he carries the real token by water, has the tail been lured away, or lured onto him? This route to the pier, Ah Shun’s boat, who moves about in town before daybreak—she still has to watch them all closely. It is just that this time, there is one more thing to watch: the box in his hand, and whether he is safe all along the way.

Liu Sanniang: He contradicted her to her face, calling her “muddled.” She may not have been convinced inwardly, but it only turned into one low curse: “Your wings have hardened, so now you think this old woman meddles too much” — without even half a measure of real anger. If someone else had said that, she would have snapped back long ago; because he said it, she took it only as an old acquaintance’s blunt temper. What ruthlessness she has remains entirely elsewhere: the ghost up north bearing Old Fifth’s name, and anyone who dares set schemes in motion on Banhuchun territory.

Liu Sanniang: His line “no one wait around for someone else to send himself to death” sounds to her more real than that earlier “Brother Lu”—being willing to take the words back up means he treats her as an old acquaintance. The final line, “do not touch it”, is said for her sake, and she notes it in her heart. It is warm, yes, but mixed into that warmth are twelve years of old accounts, and she still does not dare let it overflow.

Liu Sanniang: as the boat sways, the string in her chest tightens by another half inch—now that he is leaving, will the water route be safe? What should they bring to Wupeng Dock three days later? What is the mechanism in the empty box? In the morning fog, her face is languid, but the ledger in her heart has not stopped for a moment.

Liu Sanniang: When he boards the boat and the boat rocks, she still folds both arms across her chest and looks on coldly; she is not anxious and does not argue. At the end, she only accepts with a line, “I won’t wait for you”—the storm last night that overturned twelve years of settled conclusions, she can hold down; this line this morning, she can hold down too. She is truly steady now; it is just that beneath this steadiness presses the setup three days later, and no one knows how long it can remain steady.

Liu Sanniang: he boards the boat, and the boat rocks; she still proceeds according to her steps: listening, watching, not losing her composure because of that one line, “no one should wait for anyone else to go die.” At the fifth-watch dock, whoever panics first exposes themselves first; she knows that too well.

Liu Sanniang: His line, “No one should wait for anyone else to go get themselves killed,” amounts to acknowledging her line, “I won’t wait for you” — the scale in her heart is still twisted: if she gives the token back, the proof for Wupeng Dock three days later will no longer be in her palm; if she does not, she is slighting his face. She chose to give it, but beneath that choice there is still unwillingness pressed down.

Liu Sanniang: With his sentence "there's a mechanism in the empty box," the account book in her heart turns another page: What mechanism is inside the box? How does he plan to use the empty box to lure out the tail? What else has he been carrying along this road without telling her? These questions hook her more than whose hand the cards are in.

Liu Sanniang: His line, “No one should wait for anyone else to go die,” answered her line, “I’m not waiting for you,” and most of the breath caught in her heart eased. What remains troubling is still the deadline of “three days later”—she does not know whether three days is enough to clarify what must be clarified, or enough to draw the tail away, but she is no longer blocked up.

Liu Sanniang: the boat is about to cast off, and he is still on the dock arguing with her about the box—what she is anxious about is the hour, not having no way to go. Once the boat rocks, this string of actions is her way of seizing the time back.

Liu Sanniang: His line, “no one should wait around for someone else to go die,” is the manner of an old friend catching her earlier “I won’t wait for you.” At the end, the three words “don’t touch it” are said out of consideration for her. The door has opened a crack; inside the crack is twelve years of old friendship, while outside it each still keeps their own bottom line tucked away.

Liu Sanniang: His line “No one should wait around for someone else to throw their life away” acknowledges her line “I won’t wait for you”—the cards go to him, the box goes to her, and the boat is at her command; the initiative still leans toward her. But the dock remains her territory: the boat is tied by her, Ashun is sent by her, and the order to pole off is called by her.

Liu Sanniang: His sentence, “No one waits for anyone to go die,” is an acknowledgment of her “I won’t wait for you”—that step where she crossed the line has been taken back, but she still feels somewhat uneasy inside: it was not an outsider stepping on her threshold, but she herself who reached out, and was gently blocked back by him. She accepts this layer, but not gladly.

Liu Sanniang: He boards the boat, and the boat is about to cast off; she has no intention of relying on him to make decisions for her—whether to give the tile, whether to keep the box, whether the boat should be ordered to depart, every step is her own. In this muddy water, what she agreed to was going together, not depending on him.

Liu Sanniang: With his line “there is a mechanism in the empty box,” she immediately weighs up the trick in her mind: are the people watching the token recognizing the token or the box? Can an empty box deceive the dog noses on both river and land routes? She snatches the box and orders A Shun to raise the pole; every movement shows her familiarity with the ways of this jianghu—whether his move is a proper stroke or a risky one, she knows in her heart.

Liu Sanniang: He put away the token and boarded the boat; that token belonged to Old Fifth, and back then she had personally hung it at his waist. The fire twelve years ago, that sworn brother, and the mole case she had suspected for twelve years were all pressed onto this token. When she slapped the token down and said, “This token was my sworn brother’s life back then”, she was peeling open another layer of that scar.

Liu Sanniang: Last night she said, "If the token stays with me, the tail will be drawn away by me," yet this morning she slapped the token back into his palm — her explanation changed. This morning she still has to open the door as usual and release the word that "at the fifth watch the bill was settled and they went south." If someone asks who has the token, answering too deeply exposes the truth, while answering too shallowly fails to match up. This shell still has to be protected.

Liu Sanniang: There is not the slightest place where the act slips; the play is still within the play—the fifth-watch dock, collecting the token and boarding, the empty-box mechanism, the fate-boat pushing off with the pole, all are things old hands in this jianghu would do.

Liu Sanniang: He has boarded, and the boat is about to cast off. Right now the most important thing is still that one matter: draw the tail away so he can go cleanly to the Earth God Temple to scout. Slapping the token back into his palm, snatching over the empty box, and ordering A-Shun to raise the pole—this string of actions is what settles the matter. On the layer of who the token belongs to, she accepts it; on the layer of drawing away the tail, she takes it on.

Liu Sanniang: after slapping the plaque back and snatching the box over, she still has to open the door as usual and recite the dishes as usual, holding up the shell of “Liu Sanniang is only an innkeeper” without a single leak. Whose hand the plaque is in, and how the tail is drawn out, all have to be handled beneath this shell—the shell cannot break.

Liu Sanniang: He boards the boat, and the boat is about to cast off. She knows clearly that the meaning of this meal has changed another layer—from 'the card is in my hand; send him onto the boat and draw the tail away,' it has been pushed back to 'the card returns to him, the box returns to me, and I draw the tail.' This interception at the fifth-watch dock has made the first step of execution settle from 'chasing the card' into 'sending the person off and drawing away the tail.'

goal_tracking.trigger_summary: At the fifth-watch dock, Liu Sanniang publicly slaps the waist token back into Lu Wenfeng's palm, snatches away the empty casket, and orders Ashun to push off with the pole and send him away by water; Lu Wenfeng accepts the token and boards the boat, responding to her line “I won't wait for you” with “no one waits for anyone else to throw their life away”, and adds, “there is a mechanism in the empty casket; it is fine if others open it, but you must not touch it”. Liu Sanniang's immediate tactical goal shifts from “keep the waist token clenched in her own hand, draw the pursuers toward her own line, and send Lu Wenfeng cleanly to the Earth God Temple to scout the way” to “return the credential to Lu Wenfeng, use the empty casket as bait to draw the pursuers toward her own line, open for business as usual to protect the shell, avoid alarming the Canal Gang's old members, and three days later go to the appointment at Wupeng Dock with the token”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Arrange the food and lodging accounts for the regulars properly, while renewing old ties through reminiscing and taking the opportunity to inquire about recent movements in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Use the empty case as bait to draw the pursuers toward his own line, and send Lu Wenfeng, token in hand, along the water route to the Earth God Temple to scout the way; at the same time, open the doors as usual and release the rumor that “at the fifth watch he had settled the bill and gone south” to protect the shell, while guarding against unfamiliar faces in the building and old members of the canal gang. Three days later, go to the appointment at Wupeng Dock by token.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greeting an old regular, arranging food and lodging, quoting and settling the bill, and catching up while asking about recent circumstances.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motivation: Liu Sanniang wants to find out who is digging into the old case at Qixia Ferry, why the waist token that should have sunk into the river has resurfaced, who among the people who escorted the Qinglu is still alive, whether the person in the north who calls himself Lao Wu is real or fake, which group has pursued them to town, and whether Lu Wenfeng’s return this time is related to this—but even more, she wants to personally grip the proof for attending the appointment in her own palm, and decide for herself how this game will proceed. But this is only an inference, not yet confirmed by independent evidence.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng states that "what I ran into wasn't a hard case, but some people digging up old accounts," and directly asks, "Has anyone recently been asking about the old survivors of the battle at Qixia Ferry?"—directly touching the old case Liu Sanniang has not mentioned to anyone for twelve years.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng pushed one layer further: he asked about "the person who escorted the Qinglu across the ferry back then," showed "the Canal Gang waist token that should have sunk into the river with the corpse," and asserted that "on the night at Qixia Ferry, perhaps someone did not die at all"—pushing the old case from "someone is asking around" to "someone did not die, and physical evidence has appeared."

In her early years, Liu Sanniang was a female escort guard for the Canal Gang. In the battle at Qixia Ferry, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an inside traitor; the back courtyard of the inn is an unmarked message relay point, and gathering rumors has always been part of her daily routine.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang received the physical evidence through action: her fingers dug into the wood seams of the counter, her fingernail nearly snapping; she gripped Lu Wenfeng’s wrist, slammed the bronze key to the Tianzi Room heavily into his palm, lowered her voice and ordered him to “go upstairs” and bolt the door, arranged a private talk at midnight, and directly pressed, “That waist token—do you have it on you?”—she proactively shifted the conversation into a locked room, breaking a twelve-year taboo.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng confirmed “it is here” and added, “the people watching it have also arrived in town”—also handing over the layer of risk that the pursuers have already reached the doorstep, expanding what Liu Sanniang needs to understand from “whose waist token it is” to “which route the pursuers come from, and whether they are already among this hall full of guests.”

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang for the first time verbally put “guarding against the old members of the grain-transport gang” on the table—“After Old Five died, there were plenty of money-grubbing ingrates in that gang; I’m more on guard against them than you are”—which was tantamount to drawing a line, in front of Lu Wenfeng, between her old fellow disciples and the old guest before her.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng used a countersign to turn the midnight appointment into an executable trust contract (“Knock three times, pause for one breath, then knock twice”; “If it isn’t that number, I won’t open the door”), then turned back to warn her, “Sanniang, you be careful too”—for the first time expressing concern for Liu Sanniang herself, expanding the risk from the layer of physical evidence to her personally.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng’s first words upon entering were “Don’t turn the lamp brighter,” after which he immediately showed his waist token and previewed that “the person in the north also left a message”—expanding the showdown from “whose waist token is it” to “who is that northern route, and what message did they leave,” while locking this conversation into a room lit by only one dim lamp.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang snatched the waist token over with one hand; the instant her fingertips touched the eagle-claw engraving, she recognized that it was Lao Wu’s token, the special black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Tiegutang”, and even remembered the chipped corner of the token (broken off back then when Lao Wu blocked a blade for her). She pressed him with “Speak!”, demanding “That damned ghost up north—what message exactly did he bring you”—for the first time, in front of physical evidence from the old case, she actively reveals her personal relationship with the deceased, pushing the interrogation toward that line from the north.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng relayed the exact words of the person from the north without missing a single character—“What sank with the blue heron was an empty account; the living account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Wharf”—and added that the person “was missing half of his right ear and called himself Old Fifth.” At the end, he asked in return, “Would outsiders know about this scar?”—turning the old case from “someone didn’t die” into “the setup back then was itself fake,” while giving a date and place, and at the same time passing the ball of identity verification to Liu Sanniang.

At the fifth-watch dock in this turn, Liu Sanniang publicly slaps the waist token back into Lu Wenfeng's palm, takes away the empty box, and orders Ah Shun to raise the pole and send him off by water route—she actively returns the credential for going to Wupengwu to the token holder, while taking on the task of drawing away the tail, spelling out the move with "Leave the empty box to me; it's enough for me to run the dog noses in town in circles."
counter_evidence: Liu Sanniang’s response at this moment still uses greetings about food and lodging as the surface, and has not yet shown any particular urgency regarding the old case in the main hall.

What Lu Wenfeng provides are the original words and identity details, but he does not explain in whose hands he saw the waist token, whom he suspects, or which group was watching the token; this is insufficient to determine that he came on this trip specifically for the old case.

When she returned the token in public, she brushed it off with a low scolding of 'grown wings now, have you, and think your old mother meddles too much,' which might also just be an ordinary spat between old acquaintances, not necessarily a deliberate return of evidence.
alternatives: She is only casually asking after a regular customer’s recent situation out of an innkeeper’s duty and old friendship; as for “Qixia Ferry” and the “Qinglu,” she simply does not want to say much.
She is paying attention to general jianghu movements as part of the inn’s routine message relay, unrelated to the old Qixia Ferry case.

She returned the card and seized the box, but was only left unable to save face by his line, “Don’t make decisions for me”; she may not necessarily be trying to take the part of drawing out the tail onto herself.

Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Dock”, “half his right ear was missing, and he called himself Old Five”), and with “does any outsider know about this scar” he handed verification authority to Liu Sanniang. In this turn, at the fifth-watch pier, Liu Sanniang publicly returns the token, seizes the box, and orders the boat out; Lu Wenfeng takes the token and boards the boat, answering her line “I won't wait for you” with “no one should wait for anyone else to die”, and adds “there is a mechanism in the empty box; it is fine if others open it, but you must not touch it”—both sides are carrying weight connected to Qixia Ferry. original.rationale: This is the most natural direction of this round: the functional need has already been handled, Liu Sanniang has already taken the physical evidence through action and scheduled the conversation into a secret room, and in previous turns she further seized the token, recognized the token, and pressed with questions; in this turn she publicly returns the token, seizes the box, and orders the boat, solidifying the showdown into “Old Fifth’s token, a message left to the north, appointment at Wupeng Dock.” Lu Wenfeng brings the original words of the person to the north and the identity details together into this dark room; the most likely next step is that both sides each yield a little and push the thread of conversation one layer further down.

original.rationale: Liu Sanniang has protected this matter for twelve years, so the safest response is to pretend it is ordinary; Lu Wenfeng also understands propriety—if she cannot force it out, he will not force it into her hands.

paths.label: Degrade

If, during the boat journey or along the Earth God Temple line, she picks it up too hastily, or if Lu Wenfeng reads that she is too deeply implicated in this case and withdraws his line of talk, the probing will fail, and their reminiscing will regress into routine business conducted with mutual guards up.

paths.summary: The probing lost its sense of proportion, reminiscing retreated into routine business, and both sides felt that this exchange had failed to connect, each putting up defenses.

original.rationale: Both of them are carrying something weighty related to Qixia Ferry in their hearts; once their sense of propriety slips, it is easiest for them to slide into mutual defensiveness. “The person to the north also left behind a sentence” is already the closest sentence to the boundary in the current game, and seizing the token to interrogate him, then returning the token publicly while taking the box, pushes this risk up another layer.

But his line, “Only by leaving someone alive will there be someone to settle the account to the end,” struck me squarely in the rib where it hurt the most. Twelve years ago, if I too had died in the great fire at Qixia Ferry, who would be here today to reopen the case for that boatload of wronged souls?
“You’re ruthless, I’ll give you that.” I closed my eyes, forcibly choked back the evil fire in my chest, and in the end, through gritted teeth, gave a heavy nod.

“Half an incense stick. Not one breath more, or I won’t wait. We immediately withdraw back to town, close down the shop, recruit men and horses, and fight them to the death.” I stepped forward, roughly straightened your collar for you, and lowered my voice, every word as if squeezed out through my teeth. “Lu Wenfeng, you listen carefully.
