goal_tracking.trigger_summary: At the fifth-watch dock, Liu Sanniang publicly slaps the waist token back into Lu Wenfeng's palm, snatches away the empty casket, and orders Ashun to push off with the pole and send him away by water; Lu Wenfeng accepts the token and boards the boat, responding to her line “I won't wait for you” with “no one waits for anyone else to throw their life away”, and adds, “there is a mechanism in the empty casket; it is fine if others open it, but you must not touch it”. Liu Sanniang's immediate tactical goal shifts from “keep the waist token clenched in her own hand, draw the pursuers toward her own line, and send Lu Wenfeng cleanly to the Earth God Temple to scout the way” to “return the credential to Lu Wenfeng, use the empty casket as bait to draw the pursuers toward her own line, open for business as usual to protect the shell, avoid alarming the Canal Gang's old members, and three days later go to the appointment at Wupeng Dock with the token”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Arrange the food and lodging accounts for the regulars properly, while renewing old ties through reminiscing and taking the opportunity to inquire about recent movements in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Use the empty case as bait to draw the pursuers toward his own line, and send Lu Wenfeng, token in hand, along the water route to the Earth God Temple to scout the way; at the same time, open the doors as usual and release the rumor that “at the fifth watch he had settled the bill and gone south” to protect the shell, while guarding against unfamiliar faces in the building and old members of the canal gang. Three days later, go to the appointment at Wupeng Dock by token.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greeting an old regular, arranging food and lodging, quoting and settling the bill, and catching up while asking about recent circumstances.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motivation: Liu Sanniang wants to find out who is digging into the old case at Qixia Ferry, why the waist token that should have sunk into the river has resurfaced, who among the people who escorted the Qinglu is still alive, whether the person in the north who calls himself Lao Wu is real or fake, which group has pursued them to town, and whether Lu Wenfeng’s return this time is related to this—but even more, she wants to personally grip the proof for attending the appointment in her own palm, and decide for herself how this game will proceed. But this is only an inference, not yet confirmed by independent evidence.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng states that "what I ran into wasn't a hard case, but some people digging up old accounts," and directly asks, "Has anyone recently been asking about the old survivors of the battle at Qixia Ferry?"—directly touching the old case Liu Sanniang has not mentioned to anyone for twelve years.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng pushed one layer further: he asked about "the person who escorted the Qinglu across the ferry back then," showed "the Canal Gang waist token that should have sunk into the river with the corpse," and asserted that "on the night at Qixia Ferry, perhaps someone did not die at all"—pushing the old case from "someone is asking around" to "someone did not die, and physical evidence has appeared."

In her early years, Liu Sanniang was a female escort guard for the Canal Gang. In the battle at Qixia Ferry, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an inside traitor; the back courtyard of the inn is an unmarked message relay point, and gathering rumors has always been part of her daily routine.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang received the physical evidence through action: her fingers dug into the wood seams of the counter, her fingernail nearly snapping; she gripped Lu Wenfeng’s wrist, slammed the bronze key to the Tianzi Room heavily into his palm, lowered her voice and ordered him to “go upstairs” and bolt the door, arranged a private talk at midnight, and directly pressed, “That waist token—do you have it on you?”—she proactively shifted the conversation into a locked room, breaking a twelve-year taboo.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng confirmed “it is here” and added, “the people watching it have also arrived in town”—also handing over the layer of risk that the pursuers have already reached the doorstep, expanding what Liu Sanniang needs to understand from “whose waist token it is” to “which route the pursuers come from, and whether they are already among this hall full of guests.”

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang for the first time verbally put “guarding against the old members of the grain-transport gang” on the table—“After Old Five died, there were plenty of money-grubbing ingrates in that gang; I’m more on guard against them than you are”—which was tantamount to drawing a line, in front of Lu Wenfeng, between her old fellow disciples and the old guest before her.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng used a countersign to turn the midnight appointment into an executable trust contract (“Knock three times, pause for one breath, then knock twice”; “If it isn’t that number, I won’t open the door”), then turned back to warn her, “Sanniang, you be careful too”—for the first time expressing concern for Liu Sanniang herself, expanding the risk from the layer of physical evidence to her personally.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng’s first words upon entering were “Don’t turn the lamp brighter,” after which he immediately showed his waist token and previewed that “the person in the north also left a message”—expanding the showdown from “whose waist token is it” to “who is that northern route, and what message did they leave,” while locking this conversation into a room lit by only one dim lamp.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang snatched the waist token over with one hand; the instant her fingertips touched the eagle-claw engraving, she recognized that it was Lao Wu’s token, the special black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Tiegutang”, and even remembered the chipped corner of the token (broken off back then when Lao Wu blocked a blade for her). She pressed him with “Speak!”, demanding “That damned ghost up north—what message exactly did he bring you”—for the first time, in front of physical evidence from the old case, she actively reveals her personal relationship with the deceased, pushing the interrogation toward that line from the north.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng relayed the exact words of the person from the north without missing a single character—“What sank with the blue heron was an empty account; the living account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Wharf”—and added that the person “was missing half of his right ear and called himself Old Fifth.” At the end, he asked in return, “Would outsiders know about this scar?”—turning the old case from “someone didn’t die” into “the setup back then was itself fake,” while giving a date and place, and at the same time passing the ball of identity verification to Liu Sanniang.

At the fifth-watch dock in this turn, Liu Sanniang publicly slaps the waist token back into Lu Wenfeng's palm, takes away the empty box, and orders Ah Shun to raise the pole and send him off by water route—she actively returns the credential for going to Wupengwu to the token holder, while taking on the task of drawing away the tail, spelling out the move with "Leave the empty box to me; it's enough for me to run the dog noses in town in circles."
counter_evidence: Liu Sanniang’s response at this moment still uses greetings about food and lodging as the surface, and has not yet shown any particular urgency regarding the old case in the main hall.

What Lu Wenfeng provides are the original words and identity details, but he does not explain in whose hands he saw the waist token, whom he suspects, or which group was watching the token; this is insufficient to determine that he came on this trip specifically for the old case.

When she returned the token in public, she brushed it off with a low scolding of 'grown wings now, have you, and think your old mother meddles too much,' which might also just be an ordinary spat between old acquaintances, not necessarily a deliberate return of evidence.
alternatives: She is only casually asking after a regular customer’s recent situation out of an innkeeper’s duty and old friendship; as for “Qixia Ferry” and the “Qinglu,” she simply does not want to say much.
She is paying attention to general jianghu movements as part of the inn’s routine message relay, unrelated to the old Qixia Ferry case.

She returned the card and seized the box, but was only left unable to save face by his line, “Don’t make decisions for me”; she may not necessarily be trying to take the part of drawing out the tail onto herself.

In present, Lu Wenfeng has already handed over the physical-evidence layer (the Qinglu, the waist token, “someone isn't dead”); the previous turn confirmed that the waist token was on him and that pursuers had already reached the town, and further delivered both the original words and identity details of the person to the north (“what sank with the Qinglu was the empty account; the live account is still there. In this turn, at the fifth-watch pier, Liu Sanniang publicly returns the token, seizes the box, and orders the boat out; Lu Wenfeng takes the token and boards the boat, answering her line “I won't wait for you” with “no one should wait for anyone else to die”, and adds “there is a mechanism in the empty box; it is fine if others open it, but you must not touch it”—both sides are carrying weight connected to Qixia Ferry. Lu Wenfeng receives her response and is willing to reveal another layer—for example, explaining in whose hands he saw the waist token, or accounting for which side is watching the token, or pointing out why he is certain that ‘someone is not dead.’
paths.summary: The reminiscing advances to a limited exchange of information around the authenticity of ‘Old Fifth’ and that waist token. Each side reveals a little of what they know, and both their relationship and the information move one step forward, but neither hands over the bottom line.

original.rationale: This is the most natural direction of this round: the functional need has already been handled, Liu Sanniang has already taken the physical evidence through action and scheduled the conversation into a secret room, and in previous turns she further seized the token, recognized the token, and pressed with questions; in this turn she publicly returns the token, seizes the box, and orders the boat, solidifying the showdown into “Old Fifth’s token, a message left to the north, appointment at Wupeng Dock.” Lu Wenfeng brings the original words of the person to the north and the identity details together into this dark room; the most likely next step is that both sides each yield a little and push the thread of conversation one layer further down.

paths.label: Maintain

If during the boat trip or along the Earth God Temple line Lu Wenfeng still refuses to say where the northern remark came from and only fobs her off with “look at the plaque first,” then when she sees that she cannot force it out of him, she will stop pressing and instead arrange for him to rest and eat. paths.summary: The greeting is proper, old acquaintances reconnect, physical evidence is brought to the threshold of a taboo and then gently covered back up; both sides keep something in reserve, and the old case is not pursued further.

original.rationale: Liu Sanniang has protected this matter for twelve years, so the safest response is to pretend it is ordinary; Lu Wenfeng also understands propriety—if she cannot force it out, he will not force it into her hands.

paths.label: Degrade
paths.reasoning_trace: The "Qinglu" and that waist token carried enormous weight for Liu Sanniang. In the previous turn she had already seized the token, recognized it, and interrogated him, laying bare twelve years of taboo to his face; in this turn she publicly returns the token, seizes the box, and orders the boat out, putting the split-up operation openly on the table. If, during the boat journey or along the Earth God Temple line, she picks it up too hastily, or if Lu Wenfeng reads that she is too deeply implicated in this case and withdraws his line of talk, the probing will fail, and their reminiscing will regress into routine business conducted with mutual guards up.
requirements: When pressing about that line concerning the north, Liu Sanniang shows obvious avoidance or an unnatural expression, or questions too urgently and gives herself away
After Lu Wenfeng notices, he may press further or withdraw the thread; both sides then shift into routine responses discussing only room money and meal money.
paths.summary: The probing lost its sense of proportion, reminiscing retreated into routine business, and both sides felt that this exchange had failed to connect, each putting up defenses.

original.rationale: Both of them are carrying something weighty related to Qixia Ferry in their hearts; once their sense of propriety slips, it is easiest for them to slide into mutual defensiveness. “The person to the north also left behind a sentence” is already the closest sentence to the boundary in the current game, and seizing the token to interrogate him, then returning the token publicly while taking the box, pushes this risk up another layer.

plot_point: At the fifth watch, at the backyard dock: in front of everyone, Liu Sanniang slapped the black-iron waist token back into Lu Wenfeng’s palm, then seized the empty case from his hand and ordered the boatman Ashun to pole off and send him away by water.

The reason Liu Sanniang gives is: the token is a death warrant; if he carries it, the dog noses on both water and land routes can catch the scent and chase him. Leaving the empty box with her is enough to lead the dog noses in town round and round.

Liu Sanniang settles both the returning of the plaque and the harsh words with, "Old friendship is old friendship, but remember this: that plaque was my sworn brother's life back then. When it comes to settling this debt, I am more qualified than you. If you die halfway, no one will collect your corpse for you." She also sets the rule for meeting with, "At the Earth God Temple. If you're late, this old woman won't wait for you."

Lu Wenfeng puts away the waist token and steps onto the small boat, accepting her line “I won’t wait for you” with “Just what I wanted—no one waits for anyone to get killed,” and then adds, “There’s a mechanism in the empty box. It’s fine if others open it; you mustn’t touch it”—laying bare the workings of the empty box to her while warning her not to touch it.

The suspended layer of voucher ownership has landed—the token is back in Lu Wenfeng’s hand—and the step of drawing out the tail has been handed back to Liu Sanniang—the empty box is in her hand. But “why she took it without telling anyone last night,” “what to take to Wupeng Dock three days later,” and “how her line will draw out the tail” remain unresolved, with the new added layer that “the empty box has a mechanism; do not touch it.”

This route to the pier, Ah Shun’s boat, who moves about in town before daybreak—she still has to watch them all closely. Lu Wenfeng: She returns the token, seizes the box, and commands the boat in public, yet he still proceeds at his own pace: listening, watching, leaving room in his words. Her return and seizure determine what he gives next—whether to board the boat and leave, or to ask one layer deeper.

goal_tracking.trigger_summary: At the fifth-watch dock, Liu Sanniang publicly slaps the waist token back into Lu Wenfeng's palm, snatches away the empty casket, and orders Ashun to push off with the pole and send him away by water; Lu Wenfeng accepts the token and boards the boat, responding to her line “I won't wait for you” with “no one waits for anyone else to throw their life away”, and adds, “there is a mechanism in the empty casket; it is fine if others open it, but you must not touch it”. Liu Sanniang's immediate tactical goal shifts from “keep the waist token clenched in her own hand, draw the pursuers toward her own line, and send Lu Wenfeng cleanly to the Earth God Temple to scout the way” to “return the credential to Lu Wenfeng, use the empty casket as bait to draw the pursuers toward her own line, open for business as usual to protect the shell, avoid alarming the Canal Gang's old members, and three days later go to the appointment at Wupeng Dock with the token”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Arrange the food and lodging accounts for the regulars properly, while renewing old ties through reminiscing and taking the opportunity to inquire about recent movements in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Use the empty case as bait to draw the pursuers toward his own line, and send Lu Wenfeng, token in hand, along the water route to the Earth God Temple to scout the way; at the same time, open the doors as usual and release the rumor that “at the fifth watch he had settled the bill and gone south” to protect the shell, while guarding against unfamiliar faces in the building and old members of the canal gang. Three days later, go to the appointment at Wupeng Dock by token.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greeting an old regular, arranging food and lodging, quoting and settling the bill, and catching up while asking about recent circumstances.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motivation: Liu Sanniang wants to find out who is digging into the old case at Qixia Ferry, why the waist token that should have sunk into the river has resurfaced, who among the people who escorted the Qinglu is still alive, whether the person in the north who calls himself Lao Wu is real or fake, which group has pursued them to town, and whether Lu Wenfeng’s return this time is related to this—but even more, she wants to personally grip the proof for attending the appointment in her own palm, and decide for herself how this game will proceed. But this is only an inference, not yet confirmed by independent evidence.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng states that "what I ran into wasn't a hard case, but some people digging up old accounts," and directly asks, "Has anyone recently been asking about the old survivors of the battle at Qixia Ferry?"—directly touching the old case Liu Sanniang has not mentioned to anyone for twelve years.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng pushed one layer further: he asked about "the person who escorted the Qinglu across the ferry back then," showed "the Canal Gang waist token that should have sunk into the river with the corpse," and asserted that "on the night at Qixia Ferry, perhaps someone did not die at all"—pushing the old case from "someone is asking around" to "someone did not die, and physical evidence has appeared."

In her early years, Liu Sanniang was a female escort guard for the Canal Gang. In the battle at Qixia Ferry, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an inside traitor; the back courtyard of the inn is an unmarked message relay point, and gathering rumors has always been part of her daily routine.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang received the physical evidence through action: her fingers dug into the wood seams of the counter, her fingernail nearly snapping; she gripped Lu Wenfeng’s wrist, slammed the bronze key to the Tianzi Room heavily into his palm, lowered her voice and ordered him to “go upstairs” and bolt the door, arranged a private talk at midnight, and directly pressed, “That waist token—do you have it on you?”—she proactively shifted the conversation into a locked room, breaking a twelve-year taboo.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng confirmed “it is here” and added, “the people watching it have also arrived in town”—also handing over the layer of risk that the pursuers have already reached the doorstep, expanding what Liu Sanniang needs to understand from “whose waist token it is” to “which route the pursuers come from, and whether they are already among this hall full of guests.”

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang for the first time verbally put “guarding against the old members of the grain-transport gang” on the table—“After Old Five died, there were plenty of money-grubbing ingrates in that gang; I’m more on guard against them than you are”—which was tantamount to drawing a line, in front of Lu Wenfeng, between her old fellow disciples and the old guest before her.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng used a countersign to turn the midnight appointment into an executable trust contract (“Knock three times, pause for one breath, then knock twice”; “If it isn’t that number, I won’t open the door”), then turned back to warn her, “Sanniang, you be careful too”—for the first time expressing concern for Liu Sanniang herself, expanding the risk from the layer of physical evidence to her personally.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng’s first words upon entering were “Don’t turn the lamp brighter,” after which he immediately showed his waist token and previewed that “the person in the north also left a message”—expanding the showdown from “whose waist token is it” to “who is that northern route, and what message did they leave,” while locking this conversation into a room lit by only one dim lamp.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang snatched the waist token over with one hand; the instant her fingertips touched the eagle-claw engraving, she recognized that it was Lao Wu’s token, the special black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Tiegutang”, and even remembered the chipped corner of the token (broken off back then when Lao Wu blocked a blade for her). She pressed him with “Speak!”, demanding “That damned ghost up north—what message exactly did he bring you”—for the first time, in front of physical evidence from the old case, she actively reveals her personal relationship with the deceased, pushing the interrogation toward that line from the north.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng relayed the exact words of the person from the north without missing a single character—“What sank with the blue heron was an empty account; the living account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Wharf”—and added that the person “was missing half of his right ear and called himself Old Fifth.” At the end, he asked in return, “Would outsiders know about this scar?”—turning the old case from “someone didn’t die” into “the setup back then was itself fake,” while giving a date and place, and at the same time passing the ball of identity verification to Liu Sanniang.

At the fifth-watch dock in this turn, Liu Sanniang publicly slaps the waist token back into Lu Wenfeng's palm, takes away the empty box, and orders Ah Shun to raise the pole and send him off by water route—she actively returns the credential for going to Wupengwu to the token holder, while taking on the task of drawing away the tail, spelling out the move with "Leave the empty box to me; it's enough for me to run the dog noses in town in circles."
counter_evidence: Liu Sanniang’s response at this moment still uses greetings about food and lodging as the surface, and has not yet shown any particular urgency regarding the old case in the main hall.

What Lu Wenfeng provides are the original words and identity details, but he does not explain in whose hands he saw the waist token, whom he suspects, or which group was watching the token; this is insufficient to determine that he came on this trip specifically for the old case.

When she returned the token in public, she brushed it off with a low scolding of 'grown wings now, have you, and think your old mother meddles too much,' which might also just be an ordinary spat between old acquaintances, not necessarily a deliberate return of evidence.
alternatives: She is only casually asking after a regular customer’s recent situation out of an innkeeper’s duty and old friendship; as for “Qixia Ferry” and the “Qinglu,” she simply does not want to say much.
She is paying attention to general jianghu movements as part of the inn’s routine message relay, unrelated to the old Qixia Ferry case.

She returned the card and seized the box, but was only left unable to save face by his line, “Don’t make decisions for me”; she may not necessarily be trying to take the part of drawing out the tail onto herself.

paths.label: Advance
paths.reasoning_trace: In past, Liu Sanniang and Lu Wenfeng have been old acquaintances for many years, and she came from a grain-transport gang in her early years; the back courtyard has always been a message relay point. In present, Lu Wenfeng has already handed over the physical-evidence layer (the Qinglu, the waist token, “someone isn't dead”); the previous turn confirmed that the waist token was on him and that pursuers had already reached the town, and further delivered both the original words and identity details of the person to the north (“what sank with the Qinglu was the empty account; the live account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Dock”, “half his right ear was missing, and he called himself Old Five”), and with “does any outsider know about this scar” he handed verification authority to Liu Sanniang. In this turn, at the fifth-watch pier, Liu Sanniang publicly returns the token, seizes the box, and orders the boat out; Lu Wenfeng takes the token and boards the boat, answering her line “I won't wait for you” with “no one should wait for anyone else to die”, and adds “there is a mechanism in the empty box; it is fine if others open it, but you must not touch it”—both sides are carrying weight connected to Qixia Ferry. The conversation has already moved beyond sounding each other out; physical evidence and the truth or falsity of identities have been laid out, and the midnight private talk, entry method, separate actions, and rendezvous rules have already been arranged. If, during the boat journey or along the Earth God Temple line, she is willing to reveal a little about that scar and he is willing to expose another layer, then catching up on old times will advance into a limited but substantive exchange of information.

Lu Wenfeng receives her response and is willing to reveal another layer—for example, explaining in whose hands he saw the waist token, or accounting for which side is watching the token, or pointing out why he is certain that ‘someone is not dead.’
paths.summary: The reminiscing advances to a limited exchange of information around the authenticity of ‘Old Fifth’ and that waist token. Each side reveals a little of what they know, and both their relationship and the information move one step forward, but neither hands over the bottom line.

original.rationale: This is the most natural direction of this round: the functional need has already been handled, Liu Sanniang has already taken the physical evidence through action and scheduled the conversation into a secret room, and in previous turns she further seized the token, recognized the token, and pressed with questions; in this turn she publicly returns the token, seizes the box, and orders the boat, solidifying the showdown into “Old Fifth’s token, a message left to the north, appointment at Wupeng Dock.” Lu Wenfeng brings the original words of the person to the north and the identity details together into this dark room; the most likely next step is that both sides each yield a little and push the thread of conversation one layer further down.

paths.label: Advance

If Lu Wenfeng boards the boat as told and leaves by water, while Liu Sanniang opens the door as usual and lets out the word that 'the bill was settled at the fifth watch and he headed south,' then this turn makes the first step of execution settle from 'pursuing the badge' into 'sending the person away and drawing the tail,' advancing the interaction into a new situation that can be explained by what has already happened.
requirements: Lu Wenfeng accepts the arrangement that ‘the token goes to me, the box goes to you, and you draw the tail,’ boards the boat, and takes the water route to scout the way to the Earth God Temple.
Liu Sanniang opens the door as usual and lets out the word that "the account was settled at the fifth watch and they went south," drawing the pursuers' attention onto her own line.
paths.summary: The split action is implemented: Lu Wenfeng carries the token and travels light, taking the water route ahead to scout; Liu Sanniang holds the empty box and stays in town to draw off the pursuers, opening the door as usual to protect the shell. They will meet again at Wupeng Dock three days later.

original.rationale: Liu Sanniang has already arranged the boat, A Shun, and the line to take. Lu Wenfeng's request to have the waist token returned was originally to preserve a credential for the appointment. She returns the token publicly and gives the reason "leave the empty box to me; that is enough for me to lead the dog noses in town around in circles," which aligns with his own calculations, so he is most likely to board the boat accordingly.

paths.label: Maintain
paths.reasoning_trace: In the present, although Liu Sanniang returns the plaque, seizes the box, and orders the boat, she has guarded this matter extremely steadily for twelve years. If during the boat trip or along the Earth God Temple line Lu Wenfeng still refuses to say where the northern remark came from and only fobs her off with “look at the plaque first,” then when she sees that she cannot force it out of him, she will stop pressing and instead arrange for him to rest and eat. This turn would then stop at proper hospitality plus a layer of vague rumor: the friendship is resumed, and the old case does not deepen further.
requirements: Lu Wenfeng does not answer where that remark about the north came from, only putting it off with “look at the token first” or “we’ll talk tomorrow.”
Seeing that she cannot force anything out of him, Liu Sanniang stops pressing and instead starts arranging for him to rest, or pulls the topic back to room fees and meal money.
paths.summary: The greeting is proper, old acquaintances reconnect, physical evidence is brought to the threshold of a taboo and then gently covered back up; both sides keep something in reserve, and the old case is not pursued further.

original.rationale: Liu Sanniang has protected this matter for twelve years, so the safest response is to pretend it is ordinary; Lu Wenfeng also understands propriety—if she cannot force it out, he will not force it into her hands.

paths.label: Degrade
paths.reasoning_trace: The "Qinglu" and that waist token carried enormous weight for Liu Sanniang. In the previous turn she had already seized the token, recognized it, and interrogated him, laying bare twelve years of taboo to his face; in this turn she publicly returns the token, seizes the box, and orders the boat out, putting the split-up operation openly on the table. If, during the boat journey or along the Earth God Temple line, she picks it up too hastily, or if Lu Wenfeng reads that she is too deeply implicated in this case and withdraws his line of talk, the probing will fail, and their reminiscing will regress into routine business conducted with mutual guards up.
requirements: When pressing about that line concerning the north, Liu Sanniang shows obvious avoidance or an unnatural expression, or questions too urgently and gives herself away
After Lu Wenfeng notices, he may press further or withdraw the thread; both sides then shift into routine responses discussing only room money and meal money.
paths.summary: The probing lost its sense of proportion, reminiscing retreated into routine business, and both sides felt that this exchange had failed to connect, each putting up defenses.

original.rationale: Both of them are carrying something weighty related to Qixia Ferry in their hearts; once their sense of propriety slips, it is easiest for them to slide into mutual defensiveness. “The person to the north also left behind a sentence” is already the closest sentence to the boundary in the current game, and seizing the token to interrogate him, then returning the token publicly while taking the box, pushes this risk up another layer.

evidence.quote: I froze, then gave a low spit of embarrassment and anger, raising my hand to smack myself on the forehead. “Tsk, this brain of mine today—truly clouded by lard. I even missed such obvious life gates and death positions. Fine, as you say, Rocky Slope!”

I reined in the embarrassment on my face, my gaze turning cold and steady in an instant. I made a gesture to you for splitting up, and lowered my voice: “You guard the east, I’ll guard the west. If anyone comes, just recognize the face. I’ll keep this account in my head first and absolutely won’t act rashly. If there really is a second group of orioles behind the mantis… hmph, imitate a water duck’s call, is it? Don’t you go mistaking my voice. Be careful in everything.”

With that, I lowered my body, like a gray feral cat hugging the ground, and moved soundlessly along the blind corner behind the temple wall toward Rocky Slope downwind. In the blink of an eye, I had hidden myself among the shadows of the rocks and withered grass.

In her early years, Liu Sanniang was a female escort guard for the Canal Gang. In the battle at Qixia Ferry, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an inside traitor; the back courtyard of the inn is an unmarked message relay point, and gathering rumors has always been part of her daily routine.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng confirmed “it is here” and added, “the people watching it have also arrived in town”—also handing over the layer of risk that the pursuers have already reached the doorstep, expanding what Liu Sanniang needs to understand from “whose waist token it is” to “which route the pursuers come from, and whether they are already among this hall full of guests.”

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang for the first time verbally put “guarding against the old members of the grain-transport gang” on the table—“After Old Five died, there were plenty of money-grubbing ingrates in that gang; I’m more on guard against them than you are”—which was tantamount to drawing a line, in front of Lu Wenfeng, between her old fellow disciples and the old guest before her.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng used a countersign to turn the midnight appointment into an executable trust contract (“Knock three times, pause for one breath, then knock twice”; “If it isn’t that number, I won’t open the door”), then turned back to warn her, “Sanniang, you be careful too”—for the first time expressing concern for Liu Sanniang herself, expanding the risk from the layer of physical evidence to her personally.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng’s first words upon entering were “Don’t turn the lamp brighter,” after which he immediately showed his waist token and previewed that “the person in the north also left a message”—expanding the showdown from “whose waist token is it” to “who is that northern route, and what message did they leave,” while locking this conversation into a room lit by only one dim lamp.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang snatched the waist token over with one hand; the instant her fingertips touched the eagle-claw engraving, she recognized that it was Lao Wu’s token, the special black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Tiegutang”, and even remembered the chipped corner of the token (broken off back then when Lao Wu blocked a blade for her). She pressed him with “Speak!”, demanding “That damned ghost up north—what message exactly did he bring you”—for the first time, in front of physical evidence from the old case, she actively reveals her personal relationship with the deceased, pushing the interrogation toward that line from the north.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng relayed the exact words of the person from the north without missing a single character—“What sank with the blue heron was an empty account; the living account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Wharf”—and added that the person “was missing half of his right ear and called himself Old Fifth.” At the end, he asked in return, “Would outsiders know about this scar?”—turning the old case from “someone didn’t die” into “the setup back then was itself fake,” while giving a date and place, and at the same time passing the ball of identity verification to Liu Sanniang.

In this turn at the Earth God Temple, Liu Sanniang matches the code with “three, one, two,” states that she used an empty case to lure the watchers tailing her to the rocky shoal to the south, and recognizes “three reds against the current, same sect avoids the edge” and the “two short, one long” “night-crossing watch.” She also discloses Ironbone Hall’s reply coded mark: “broken reed tied with black thread, pointed finger in mud and sand”—for the first time, she actively tells outsiders the old rules and old codes of Ironbone Hall, breaking the old precedent of “old cases and old rules are not spoken of to others.”

engagement.user_interest_reading: Liu Sanniang appears at the Earth God Temple as promised—the line from the dock three days ago, “Meet at the Earth God Temple,” did not fall through; the code matches perfectly, and she even actively reports what she found from scouting Wupengwu (the water surface is eerily still; there is definitely a trap). In this turn, she further lays out in full the old rule of Tiegutang, “Three reds against the current; fellow disciples avoid the edge,” as well as the hidden mark for a reply (“broken reed bound with black thread, tip pointing to mud and sand”), and sets the action direction of “feeling our way over from underwater.” She also adds, “If you don’t come back by the appointed time, this old woman will absolutely not flee alone.” Given her personality of low extraversion, avoidant attachment, and medium engagement_sensitivity, “she is willing to come, willing to take responsibility, keeps the appointment, gives him the inside information, and stakes her life on it” is what can best maintain his interest. With Wupengwu imminent, he still needs this line of hers. Therefore, it is maintained at 0.95.
engagement.tolerance_reading: The scene requires the innkeeper to be reliable, keep secrets, and deliver messages with a sense of proportion. In this turn, while lying in wait at Luanshi Slope, Liu Sanniang personally confirms that the man in the bamboo hat cuts away the black thread, has an old burn on his right wrist, yet is wearing official boots. From behind the rocks, she signals to Lu Wenfeng "only watch, don't pursue"—she upholds his rule of "watch separately, identify only the face, don't act," does not pursue on her own, does not make a sound and expose herself, and does not overstep by taking over the judgment. Once the official boots appear, this game is deeper than previously estimated, and the risk exposure has not disappeared, but her handling still meets the scene requirements. Tolerance remains 0.40.

plot_point: Three days later, at the Earth God Temple: Lu Wenfeng arrives first and only emerges from behind the shrine after hearing footsteps, demanding the signal and asking whether the area behind is clean. Liu Sanniang knocks the pillar with “three, one, two” to match the signal, states that she used an empty case to lead the watchers to the rocky beach in the south, and reports what she learned from scouting the route—Wupeng Dock’s water surface is eerily still, without even a single waterbird; there is absolutely a trap.

Lu Wenfeng reports that three red strings tied against the current in the reeds are an old warning method of the Canal Gang; Liu Sanniang recognizes this as the old rule of Tiegu Hall, "Three reds against the current; fellow members avoid the edge," something that would never be lightly revealed unless the hall faced utter disaster, and Lao Wu back then was precisely the deputy hall master of Tiegu Hall—therefore determining that in the dock, either Lao Wu is giving a warning, or someone has thoroughly figured out Tiegu Hall's inside details and set a trap.

Liu Sanniang proposes entering the rear hold from underwater. Lu Wenfeng restrains her with “since it is a fellow sect member avoiding the edge and warning us, wouldn’t entering through the water waste the warning-giver’s intentions?” and instead suggests first checking whether the rope knots are new or old, then asks whether Tiegu Hall has any reply cipher after seeing the three reds. Liu Sanniang answers that there is—“bent reeds bound with black thread, the tip pointing to mud and sand”—and admits that just now she nearly lost her sense of proportion.

Lu Wenfeng set the division of labor: he took the black thread to test the rope and leave a mark, while Liu Sanniang would stay in the temple to watch the rear route; if he did not return within half an incense stick, she would withdraw. Liu Sanniang at first refused the order to withdraw alone, but Lu Wenfeng cornered her with “If you won’t agree to withdraw, then I won’t go”. In the end, she nodded and agreed with “half an incense stick; I won’t wait even one breath longer”, and left behind the words “your life is now entered on my account book”.

Lu Wenfeng darts out of the temple gate to inspect the ropes, while Liu Sanniang flips up onto the roof of the Earth God Temple to lie in wait, silently counting the hours, one hand on the short blade kept close to her body; in less than half an incense stick’s time, Lu Wenfeng flips back in through the rear window and reports: "The knots are new, and cinnabar sticks to the hand. As soon as the black threads were tied on, two short knocks and one long knock against a boat sounded from the fort—someone is waiting for us, and someone is also watching those three ropes."

Liu Sanniang recognizes “two short, one long” as the “night-crossing signal” of Tiegu Hall from back then, and judges that the person in the dock is either Lao Wu or someone who has set a trap after thoroughly figuring out Lao Wu's background. She immediately wants to slip through the rear ditch into the dock; Lu Wenfeng stops her with “the knocking is both a reply and a way to tell the watchers that the fish has arrived,” and instead proposes first withdrawing from the net and watching the red cord to see who comes to take the black thread.

Liu Sanniang first proposed retreating to the old locust tree behind the temple. Lu Wenfeng rejected it with, “The old locust tree is a ready-made lookout point; the other side won’t fail to notice it,” and instead set the retreat at the leeward rocky slope: split up to watch, identify newcomers only by face and do not strike, and if a second group appears, imitate a water duck once and withdraw at once. Liu Sanniang acknowledged that she had overlooked the living gate and death position, and followed his instructions to split off and move stealthily, guarding the west side.

This turn: after the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, Lu Wenfeng sees a traveler in a bamboo hat cut away a black thread; the exposed right wrist has an old burn scar, but the feet are in official boots, and from across the rubble the traveler signals to Liu Sanniang: “watch only, don’t pursue.”
attention: Liu Sanniang: she held to the “watch separately” that he had set. Now that the conical-hat guest has appeared, she gestures to him across the rubble, “watch only, do not pursue”—passing the authority to judge over to him, and trusting that he can take it. Trust is trust, but once official boots appear, another layer of weighing is added to that trust: this game is deeper than the two of them estimated; whoever exposes themselves first dies first.

Liu Sanniang: The bamboo-hatted guest cut away the black thread, had an old burn on his right wrist, yet wore official boots on his feet—all four things enter her eyes at once, and she lies among the jagged rocks suppressing even her breathing. Official boots mean that people from the authorities have already touched this thread, and the fact that the other party recognizes the black thread and dares to come take it means the line watching the rope is tougher than previously estimated. At this moment, in her eyes, not one place is safe.

Liu Sanniang's immediate tactical objective has been adjusted from “send Lu Wenfeng with the token along the water route to the Land Temple to scout the way, while keeping the doors open as usual to protect the shell” to “meet Lu Wenfeng at the Land Temple, compare the clues each of them has found, guard the red rope and see who comes to take the black thread, only watch and do not pursue, figure out the identity of the person setting the trap (especially the layer involving the official boots), and only then decide how to enter Wupengwu”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Arrange the food and lodging accounts for the regulars properly, while renewing old ties through reminiscing and taking the opportunity to inquire about recent movements in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Meet Lu Wenfeng at the Land Temple and compare the clues they have each uncovered; keep watch over the red cord to see who comes to retrieve the black thread, only watching and not pursuing; find out the identity of the traveler in the bamboo hat (especially the official boots), and who made the two short, one long knocks on the boat in the dock, then decide how to enter Wupeng Dock.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greeting an old regular, arranging food and lodging, quoting and settling the bill, and catching up while asking about recent circumstances.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motive: Liu Sanniang wants to figure out who is digging into the old Qixia Ferry case, why the waist token that should have sunk into the river has resurfaced, who among those who escorted the Qinglu is still alive, whether the person in the north calling himself Fifth is real or fake, which faction has followed the trail into town, and whether Lu Wenfeng's return this time is connected to any of this—now that official boots have appeared, she is even more intent on finding out which side the official authorities stood on in the fire-fight twelve years ago. But this is only an inference, and there is not yet independent evidence to substantiate it.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng states that "what I ran into wasn't a hard case, but some people digging up old accounts," and directly asks, "Has anyone recently been asking about the old survivors of the battle at Qixia Ferry?"—directly touching the old case Liu Sanniang has not mentioned to anyone for twelve years.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng pushed one layer further: he asked about "the person who escorted the Qinglu across the ferry back then," showed "the Canal Gang waist token that should have sunk into the river with the corpse," and asserted that "on the night at Qixia Ferry, perhaps someone did not die at all"—pushing the old case from "someone is asking around" to "someone did not die, and physical evidence has appeared."

In her early years, Liu Sanniang was a female escort guard for the Canal Gang. In the battle at Qixia Ferry, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an inside traitor; the back courtyard of the inn is an unmarked message relay point, and gathering rumors has always been part of her daily routine.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang received the physical evidence through action: her fingers dug into the wood seams of the counter, her fingernail nearly snapping; she gripped Lu Wenfeng’s wrist, slammed the bronze key to the Tianzi Room heavily into his palm, lowered her voice and ordered him to “go upstairs” and bolt the door, arranged a private talk at midnight, and directly pressed, “That waist token—do you have it on you?”—she proactively shifted the conversation into a locked room, breaking a twelve-year taboo.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng confirmed “it is here” and added, “the people watching it have also arrived in town”—also handing over the layer of risk that the pursuers have already reached the doorstep, expanding what Liu Sanniang needs to understand from “whose waist token it is” to “which route the pursuers come from, and whether they are already among this hall full of guests.”

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang for the first time verbally put “guarding against the old members of the grain-transport gang” on the table—“After Old Five died, there were plenty of money-grubbing ingrates in that gang; I’m more on guard against them than you are”—which was tantamount to drawing a line, in front of Lu Wenfeng, between her old fellow disciples and the old guest before her.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng used a countersign to turn the midnight appointment into an executable trust contract (“Knock three times, pause for one breath, then knock twice”; “If it isn’t that number, I won’t open the door”), then turned back to warn her, “Sanniang, you be careful too”—for the first time expressing concern for Liu Sanniang herself, expanding the risk from the layer of physical evidence to her personally.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng’s first words upon entering were “Don’t turn the lamp brighter,” after which he immediately showed his waist token and previewed that “the person in the north also left a message”—expanding the showdown from “whose waist token is it” to “who is that northern route, and what message did they leave,” while locking this conversation into a room lit by only one dim lamp.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang snatched the waist token over with one hand; the instant her fingertips touched the eagle-claw engraving, she recognized that it was Lao Wu’s token, the special black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Tiegutang”, and even remembered the chipped corner of the token (broken off back then when Lao Wu blocked a blade for her). She pressed him with “Speak!”, demanding “That damned ghost up north—what message exactly did he bring you”—for the first time, in front of physical evidence from the old case, she actively reveals her personal relationship with the deceased, pushing the interrogation toward that line from the north.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng relayed the exact words of the person from the north without missing a single character—“What sank with the blue heron was an empty account; the living account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Wharf”—and added that the person “was missing half of his right ear and called himself Old Fifth.” At the end, he asked in return, “Would outsiders know about this scar?”—turning the old case from “someone didn’t die” into “the setup back then was itself fake,” while giving a date and place, and at the same time passing the ball of identity verification to Liu Sanniang.

In this turn at the Earth God Temple, Liu Sanniang matches the code with “three, one, two,” states that she used an empty case to lure the watchers tailing her to the rocky shoal to the south, and recognizes “three reds against the current, same sect avoids the edge” and the “two short, one long” “night-crossing watch.” She also discloses Ironbone Hall’s reply coded mark: “broken reed tied with black thread, pointed finger in mud and sand”—for the first time, she actively tells outsiders the old rules and old codes of Ironbone Hall, breaking the old precedent of “old cases and old rules are not spoken of to others.”

After Lu Wenfeng inspected the rope and left a mark this turn, he reported back that “the straw-hat guest cut away the black thread, had an old burn scar on his right wrist, yet was wearing official boots,” and gestured “watch only, do not pursue”—for the first time, he pushes the identity clues of the person setting the trap from a jianghu gang toward the authorities, and for the first time determines the handling by gesture rather than words.
counter_evidence: Liu Sanniang's response at this moment still presents as "guard the red string, only watch and do not pursue," and has not yet shown any particular urgency about the old case on the floor of the hall.

What Lu Wenfeng offers is the appearance clue of the bamboo-hat guest, but he does not explain which route the official boots belong to, or whom he suspects, so it is insufficient to determine that this trip is specifically for the old case.

That she recognized "Three Reds Against the Current" and "Night Crossing Sentry" may simply be an instinctive reaction from her old canal-gang background, not necessarily a deliberate disclosure of old rules to an outsider.
alternatives: She is only casually asking after a regular customer’s recent situation out of an innkeeper’s duty and old friendship; as for “Qixia Ferry” and the “Qinglu,” she simply does not want to say much.
She is paying attention to general jianghu movements as part of the inn’s routine message relay, unrelated to the old Qixia Ferry case.

Her recognition of "Nishui Three Reds" and "Night Crossing Sentry" is merely an instinctive reaction from her old canal-gang background; it does not necessarily mean she intends to pursue the old case to the end.

paths.label: Advance
paths.reasoning_trace: In the past, Liu Sanniang and Lu Wenfeng had been old acquaintances for many years, and she came from the canal gang in her early years; the rear courtyard itself was already an information relay point. In the present, the two have met three days later at the Earth God Temple and matched the code. Liu Sanniang recognized “three red marks against the current, fellow disciples avoid the blade” and the “night-crossing whistle” of “two short, one long”, and also disclosed Ironbone Hall's secret marks in its reply: “broken reed tied with black thread, pointed fingers, mud and sand”. After Lu Wenfeng inspected the cord and left a mark, he reported back: “the straw-hat man cut away the black thread; old burn scar on the right wrist; but the feet wore official boots”, and signaled “watch only, do not pursue”. The straw-hat man's appearance to take the thread confirms that there is indeed someone on the line watching the cord, and “official boots” pushes the identity of the person who set the trap from jianghu gangs toward the authorities—if the two continue watching along this line, or reverse-investigate through the layer of official boots, the interaction will advance into a new situation that can be explained by what has already happened.
requirements: After taking the thread, the man in the bamboo hat does not disappear immediately, or leaves a trace that can be followed (such as the direction back to the dock, or making contact with a second group), allowing the two of them to keep watching.

paths.label: Advance
paths.reasoning_trace: In the past, Liu Sanniang recognized "Three Reds Against the Current, fellow disciples avoid the edge" and the "night-crossing signal" of "two short, one long," and judged that inside the dock either Fifth was warning them, or someone had thoroughly figured out Tiegu Hall's details and was setting a trap. paths.summary: The two of them determine that watching the line is already enough, then turn to settle on the way into Wupeng Dock, advancing the interaction from “guard the red cord and see who comes to take it” to the step of “going to the setup”.

original.rationale: The three-day deadline has arrived, and the people have reached the bureau gate. After the bamboo-hat guest takes the thread, if there is no new movement on this line, the most natural next step is to discuss how to enter Wupeng Dock; Liu Sanniang is familiar with Wupeng Dock’s terrain, and Lu Wenfeng has good qinggong. paths.label: Maintain
paths.reasoning_trace: In present, the two each hold their positions east and west, only watching and not pursuing. If there are no further movements after the bamboo-hat traveler takes the line, the two may continue lying in wait, wait for the other party to move again, or rotate surveillance and exchange observations—this turn stops at “guarding this line and waiting for the next step,” with no further deepening on the old case level.
requirements: After taking the thread, the conical-hat guest disappeared; no second group appeared, and there are no new traces to follow.
Liu Sanniang and Lu Wenfeng judge that continuing to watch still has value; they rotate or keep lying in wait, not rushing into the dock.
paths.summary: After the man in the bamboo hat takes the thread, there is no new movement; the two continue lying in wait and taking turns keeping watch, leaving this turn at 'guard this thread and wait for the next step.'

original.rationale: “Only watch, do not pursue” was the restraint Lu Wenfeng himself had set. If the bamboo-hat stranger made no new move after taking the thread, the safest response was to keep watch; though Liu Sanniang was anxious, the three-day deadline had arrived and the bureau gate was already reached, so she might not be willing to rush into the dock at this moment.

paths.label: Degrade
paths.reasoning_trace: The “official boots” layer pushes the identity of the one who set the trap toward the authorities, and it weighs heavily on Liu Sanniang—what she has suspected for twelve years is precisely an inside traitor. Now that people on the official side are involved, the scar in her heart is pulled even tighter. If she loses her composure because of the official boots, or if Lu Wenfeng reads that she is too deeply connected to this case and pulls back his line of talk, the probing will miss its mark, and the two of them will retreat into routine exchanges guarded against each other.
requirements: Liu Sanniang shows obvious avoidance or an unnatural expression at the level of “official boots,” or presses too urgently and gives herself away.
After Lu Wenfeng notices, he either presses further or withdraws the topic, and the two shift into routine coping that only discusses advance and retreat, not the old case.
paths.summary: The layer of official boots touches Liu Sanniang’s twelve-year scar; the probing loses its measure, and the two of them retreat into routine responses of mutual defensiveness.

original.rationale: The official boots expanded the doubts in the old case from “an insider” to “the authorities being involved,” precisely the layer Liu Sanniang is most sensitive to; once the measure is mishandled, it is the easiest place to slide into mutual guardedness.

goal_tracking.trigger_summary: Three days later, at the Land Temple meeting point, Liu Sanniang matched the code with “three, one, two”, stated that she had used an empty box to draw away the tail, and recognized “three reds against the current, fellow disciples avoid the edge” and the “two short, one long” “night-crossing whistle”, while also disclosing Tiegutang Hall's hidden reply mark. After Lu Wenfeng inspected the rope and left a mark, he reported back that “the man in the bamboo hat cut away the black thread, had an old burn on his right wrist, but wore official boots”, and signaled “only watch, do not pursue”. Liu Sanniang's immediate tactical objective has been adjusted from “send Lu Wenfeng with the token along the water route to the Land Temple to scout the way, while keeping the doors open as usual to protect the shell” to “meet Lu Wenfeng at the Land Temple, compare the clues each of them has found, guard the red rope and see who comes to take the black thread, only watch and do not pursue, figure out the identity of the person setting the trap (especially the layer involving the official boots), and only then decide how to enter Wupengwu”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Arrange the food and lodging accounts for the regulars properly, while renewing old ties through reminiscing and taking the opportunity to inquire about recent movements in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Meet Lu Wenfeng at the Land Temple and compare the clues they have each uncovered; keep watch over the red cord to see who comes to retrieve the black thread, only watching and not pursuing; find out the identity of the traveler in the bamboo hat (especially the official boots), and who made the two short, one long knocks on the boat in the dock, then decide how to enter Wupeng Dock.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greeting an old regular, arranging food and lodging, quoting and settling the bill, and catching up while asking about recent circumstances.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motive: Liu Sanniang wants to figure out who is digging into the old Qixia Ferry case, why the waist token that should have sunk into the river has resurfaced, who among those who escorted the Qinglu is still alive, whether the person in the north calling himself Fifth is real or fake, which faction has followed the trail into town, and whether Lu Wenfeng's return this time is connected to any of this—now that official boots have appeared, she is even more intent on finding out which side the official authorities stood on in the fire-fight twelve years ago. But this is only an inference, and there is not yet independent evidence to substantiate it.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng states that "what I ran into wasn't a hard case, but some people digging up old accounts," and directly asks, "Has anyone recently been asking about the old survivors of the battle at Qixia Ferry?"—directly touching the old case Liu Sanniang has not mentioned to anyone for twelve years.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng pushed one layer further: he asked about "the person who escorted the Qinglu across the ferry back then," showed "the Canal Gang waist token that should have sunk into the river with the corpse," and asserted that "on the night at Qixia Ferry, perhaps someone did not die at all"—pushing the old case from "someone is asking around" to "someone did not die, and physical evidence has appeared."

In her early years, Liu Sanniang was a female escort guard for the Canal Gang. In the battle at Qixia Ferry, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an inside traitor; the back courtyard of the inn is an unmarked message relay point, and gathering rumors has always been part of her daily routine.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang received the physical evidence through action: her fingers dug into the wood seams of the counter, her fingernail nearly snapping; she gripped Lu Wenfeng’s wrist, slammed the bronze key to the Tianzi Room heavily into his palm, lowered her voice and ordered him to “go upstairs” and bolt the door, arranged a private talk at midnight, and directly pressed, “That waist token—do you have it on you?”—she proactively shifted the conversation into a locked room, breaking a twelve-year taboo.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng confirmed “it is here” and added, “the people watching it have also arrived in town”—also handing over the layer of risk that the pursuers have already reached the doorstep, expanding what Liu Sanniang needs to understand from “whose waist token it is” to “which route the pursuers come from, and whether they are already among this hall full of guests.”

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang for the first time verbally put “guarding against the old members of the grain-transport gang” on the table—“After Old Five died, there were plenty of money-grubbing ingrates in that gang; I’m more on guard against them than you are”—which was tantamount to drawing a line, in front of Lu Wenfeng, between her old fellow disciples and the old guest before her.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng used a countersign to turn the midnight appointment into an executable trust contract (“Knock three times, pause for one breath, then knock twice”; “If it isn’t that number, I won’t open the door”), then turned back to warn her, “Sanniang, you be careful too”—for the first time expressing concern for Liu Sanniang herself, expanding the risk from the layer of physical evidence to her personally.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng’s first words upon entering were “Don’t turn the lamp brighter,” after which he immediately showed his waist token and previewed that “the person in the north also left a message”—expanding the showdown from “whose waist token is it” to “who is that northern route, and what message did they leave,” while locking this conversation into a room lit by only one dim lamp.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang snatched the waist token over with one hand; the instant her fingertips touched the eagle-claw engraving, she recognized that it was Lao Wu’s token, the special black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Tiegutang”, and even remembered the chipped corner of the token (broken off back then when Lao Wu blocked a blade for her). She pressed him with “Speak!”, demanding “That damned ghost up north—what message exactly did he bring you”—for the first time, in front of physical evidence from the old case, she actively reveals her personal relationship with the deceased, pushing the interrogation toward that line from the north.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng relayed the exact words of the person from the north without missing a single character—“What sank with the blue heron was an empty account; the living account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Wharf”—and added that the person “was missing half of his right ear and called himself Old Fifth.” At the end, he asked in return, “Would outsiders know about this scar?”—turning the old case from “someone didn’t die” into “the setup back then was itself fake,” while giving a date and place, and at the same time passing the ball of identity verification to Liu Sanniang.

In this turn at the Earth God Temple, Liu Sanniang matches the code with “three, one, two,” states that she used an empty case to lure the watchers tailing her to the rocky shoal to the south, and recognizes “three reds against the current, same sect avoids the edge” and the “two short, one long” “night-crossing watch.” She also discloses Ironbone Hall’s reply coded mark: “broken reed tied with black thread, pointed finger in mud and sand”—for the first time, she actively tells outsiders the old rules and old codes of Ironbone Hall, breaking the old precedent of “old cases and old rules are not spoken of to others.”

After Lu Wenfeng inspected the rope and left a mark this turn, he reported back that “the straw-hat guest cut away the black thread, had an old burn scar on his right wrist, yet was wearing official boots,” and gestured “watch only, do not pursue”—for the first time, he pushes the identity clues of the person setting the trap from a jianghu gang toward the authorities, and for the first time determines the handling by gesture rather than words.

What Lu Wenfeng offers is the appearance clue of the bamboo-hat guest, but he does not explain which route the official boots belong to, or whom he suspects, so it is insufficient to determine that this trip is specifically for the old case.

That she recognized "Three Reds Against the Current" and "Night Crossing Sentry" may simply be an instinctive reaction from her old canal-gang background, not necessarily a deliberate disclosure of old rules to an outsider.
alternatives: She is only casually asking after a regular customer’s recent situation out of an innkeeper’s duty and old friendship; as for “Qixia Ferry” and the “Qinglu,” she simply does not want to say much.
She is paying attention to general jianghu movements as part of the inn’s routine message relay, unrelated to the old Qixia Ferry case.

goal_tracking.trigger_summary: Three days later, at the Land Temple meeting point, Liu Sanniang matched the code with “three, one, two”, stated that she had used an empty box to draw away the tail, and recognized “three reds against the current, fellow disciples avoid the edge” and the “two short, one long” “night-crossing whistle”, while also disclosing Tiegutang Hall's hidden reply mark. After Lu Wenfeng inspected the rope and left a mark, he reported back that “the man in the bamboo hat cut away the black thread, had an old burn on his right wrist, but wore official boots”, and signaled “only watch, do not pursue”. Liu Sanniang's immediate tactical objective has been adjusted from “send Lu Wenfeng with the token along the water route to the Land Temple to scout the way, while keeping the doors open as usual to protect the shell” to “meet Lu Wenfeng at the Land Temple, compare the clues each of them has found, guard the red rope and see who comes to take the black thread, only watch and do not pursue, figure out the identity of the person setting the trap (especially the layer involving the official boots), and only then decide how to enter Wupengwu”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Arrange the food and lodging accounts for the regulars properly, while renewing old ties through reminiscing and taking the opportunity to inquire about recent movements in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Meet Lu Wenfeng at the Land Temple and compare the clues they have each uncovered; keep watch over the red cord to see who comes to retrieve the black thread, only watching and not pursuing; find out the identity of the traveler in the bamboo hat (especially the official boots), and who made the two short, one long knocks on the boat in the dock, then decide how to enter Wupeng Dock.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greeting an old regular, arranging food and lodging, quoting and settling the bill, and catching up while asking about recent circumstances.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motive: Liu Sanniang wants to figure out who is digging into the old Qixia Ferry case, why the waist token that should have sunk into the river has resurfaced, who among those who escorted the Qinglu is still alive, whether the person in the north calling himself Fifth is real or fake, which faction has followed the trail into town, and whether Lu Wenfeng's return this time is connected to any of this—now that official boots have appeared, she is even more intent on finding out which side the official authorities stood on in the fire-fight twelve years ago. But this is only an inference, and there is not yet independent evidence to substantiate it.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng states that "what I ran into wasn't a hard case, but some people digging up old accounts," and directly asks, "Has anyone recently been asking about the old survivors of the battle at Qixia Ferry?"—directly touching the old case Liu Sanniang has not mentioned to anyone for twelve years.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng pushed one layer further: he asked about "the person who escorted the Qinglu across the ferry back then," showed "the Canal Gang waist token that should have sunk into the river with the corpse," and asserted that "on the night at Qixia Ferry, perhaps someone did not die at all"—pushing the old case from "someone is asking around" to "someone did not die, and physical evidence has appeared."

In her early years, Liu Sanniang was a female escort guard for the Canal Gang. In the battle at Qixia Ferry, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an inside traitor; the back courtyard of the inn is an unmarked message relay point, and gathering rumors has always been part of her daily routine.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang received the physical evidence through action: her fingers dug into the wood seams of the counter, her fingernail nearly snapping; she gripped Lu Wenfeng’s wrist, slammed the bronze key to the Tianzi Room heavily into his palm, lowered her voice and ordered him to “go upstairs” and bolt the door, arranged a private talk at midnight, and directly pressed, “That waist token—do you have it on you?”—she proactively shifted the conversation into a locked room, breaking a twelve-year taboo.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng confirmed “it is here” and added, “the people watching it have also arrived in town”—also handing over the layer of risk that the pursuers have already reached the doorstep, expanding what Liu Sanniang needs to understand from “whose waist token it is” to “which route the pursuers come from, and whether they are already among this hall full of guests.”

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang for the first time verbally put “guarding against the old members of the grain-transport gang” on the table—“After Old Five died, there were plenty of money-grubbing ingrates in that gang; I’m more on guard against them than you are”—which was tantamount to drawing a line, in front of Lu Wenfeng, between her old fellow disciples and the old guest before her.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng used a countersign to turn the midnight appointment into an executable trust contract (“Knock three times, pause for one breath, then knock twice”; “If it isn’t that number, I won’t open the door”), then turned back to warn her, “Sanniang, you be careful too”—for the first time expressing concern for Liu Sanniang herself, expanding the risk from the layer of physical evidence to her personally.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng’s first words upon entering were “Don’t turn the lamp brighter,” after which he immediately showed his waist token and previewed that “the person in the north also left a message”—expanding the showdown from “whose waist token is it” to “who is that northern route, and what message did they leave,” while locking this conversation into a room lit by only one dim lamp.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang snatched the waist token over with one hand; the instant her fingertips touched the eagle-claw engraving, she recognized that it was Lao Wu’s token, the special black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Tiegutang”, and even remembered the chipped corner of the token (broken off back then when Lao Wu blocked a blade for her). She pressed him with “Speak!”, demanding “That damned ghost up north—what message exactly did he bring you”—for the first time, in front of physical evidence from the old case, she actively reveals her personal relationship with the deceased, pushing the interrogation toward that line from the north.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng relayed the exact words of the person from the north without missing a single character—“What sank with the blue heron was an empty account; the living account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Wharf”—and added that the person “was missing half of his right ear and called himself Old Fifth.” At the end, he asked in return, “Would outsiders know about this scar?”—turning the old case from “someone didn’t die” into “the setup back then was itself fake,” while giving a date and place, and at the same time passing the ball of identity verification to Liu Sanniang.

In this turn at the Earth God Temple, Liu Sanniang matches the code with “three, one, two,” states that she used an empty case to lure the watchers tailing her to the rocky shoal to the south, and recognizes “three reds against the current, same sect avoids the edge” and the “two short, one long” “night-crossing watch.” She also discloses Ironbone Hall’s reply coded mark: “broken reed tied with black thread, pointed finger in mud and sand”—for the first time, she actively tells outsiders the old rules and old codes of Ironbone Hall, breaking the old precedent of “old cases and old rules are not spoken of to others.”

After Lu Wenfeng inspected the rope and left a mark this turn, he reported back that “the straw-hat guest cut away the black thread, had an old burn scar on his right wrist, yet was wearing official boots,” and gestured “watch only, do not pursue”—for the first time, he pushes the identity clues of the person setting the trap from a jianghu gang toward the authorities, and for the first time determines the handling by gesture rather than words.
