She does not pursue anyone on her own, does not make noise and expose them, and does not overstep by taking over judgment. The layer of the official boots remains unresolved, and the second group of people wearing military-issue regulation gear adds another layer; the risk exposure has not disappeared, but her handling still fits the scene requirements. Tolerance remains at 0.40.

plot_point: Three days later, at the Earth God Temple: Lu Wenfeng arrives first and only emerges from behind the shrine after hearing footsteps, demanding the signal and asking whether the area behind is clean. Liu Sanniang knocks the pillar with “three, one, two” to match the signal, states that she used an empty case to lead the watchers to the rocky beach in the south, and reports what she learned from scouting the route—Wupeng Dock’s water surface is eerily still, without even a single waterbird; there is absolutely a trap.

Lu Wenfeng reports that three red strings tied against the current in the reeds are an old warning method of the Canal Gang; Liu Sanniang recognizes this as the old rule of Tiegu Hall, "Three reds against the current; fellow members avoid the edge," something that would never be lightly revealed unless the hall faced utter disaster, and Lao Wu back then was precisely the deputy hall master of Tiegu Hall—therefore determining that in the dock, either Lao Wu is giving a warning, or someone has thoroughly figured out Tiegu Hall's inside details and set a trap.

Liu Sanniang proposes entering the rear hold from underwater. Lu Wenfeng restrains her with “since it is a fellow sect member avoiding the edge and warning us, wouldn’t entering through the water waste the warning-giver’s intentions?” and instead suggests first checking whether the rope knots are new or old, then asks whether Tiegu Hall has any reply cipher after seeing the three reds. Liu Sanniang answers that there is—“bent reeds bound with black thread, the tip pointing to mud and sand”—and admits that just now she nearly lost her sense of proportion.

Lu Wenfeng set the division of labor: he took the black thread to test the rope and leave a mark, while Liu Sanniang would stay in the temple to watch the rear route; if he did not return within half an incense stick, she would withdraw. Liu Sanniang at first refused the order to withdraw alone, but Lu Wenfeng cornered her with “If you won’t agree to withdraw, then I won’t go”. In the end, she nodded and agreed with “half an incense stick; I won’t wait even one breath longer”, and left behind the words “your life is now entered on my account book”.

Lu Wenfeng darts out of the temple gate to inspect the ropes, while Liu Sanniang flips up onto the roof of the Earth God Temple to lie in wait, silently counting the hours, one hand on the short blade kept close to her body; in less than half an incense stick’s time, Lu Wenfeng flips back in through the rear window and reports: "The knots are new, and cinnabar sticks to the hand. As soon as the black threads were tied on, two short knocks and one long knock against a boat sounded from the fort—someone is waiting for us, and someone is also watching those three ropes."

Liu Sanniang recognizes “two short, one long” as the “night-crossing signal” of Tiegu Hall from back then, and judges that the person in the dock is either Lao Wu or someone who has set a trap after thoroughly figuring out Lao Wu's background. She immediately wants to slip through the rear ditch into the dock; Lu Wenfeng stops her with “the knocking is both a reply and a way to tell the watchers that the fish has arrived,” and instead proposes first withdrawing from the net and watching the red cord to see who comes to take the black thread.

Liu Sanniang first proposed retreating to the old locust tree behind the temple. Lu Wenfeng rejected it with, “The old locust tree is a ready-made lookout point; the other side won’t fail to notice it,” and instead set the retreat at the leeward rocky slope: split up to watch, identify newcomers only by face and do not strike, and if a second group appears, imitate a water duck once and withdraw at once. Liu Sanniang acknowledged that she had overlooked the living gate and death position, and followed his instructions to split off and move stealthily, guarding the west side.

This turn: after the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, Lu Wenfeng sees a traveler in a bamboo hat cut away a black thread; the exposed right wrist has an old burn scar, but the feet are in official boots, and from across the rubble the traveler signals to Liu Sanniang: “watch only, don’t pursue.”
attention: Liu Sanniang: she held to the “watch separately” that he had set. Now that the conical-hat guest has appeared, she gestures to him across the rubble, “watch only, do not pursue”—passing the authority to judge over to him, and trusting that he can take it. Trust is trust, but once official boots appear, another layer of weighing is added to that trust: this game is deeper than the two of them estimated; whoever exposes themselves first dies first.

Liu Sanniang: The bamboo-hatted guest cut away the black thread, had an old burn on his right wrist, yet wore official boots on his feet—all four things enter her eyes at once, and she lies among the jagged rocks suppressing even her breathing. Official boots mean that people from the authorities have already touched this thread, and the fact that the other party recognizes the black thread and dares to come take it means the line watching the rope is tougher than previously estimated. At this moment, in her eyes, not one place is safe.

Liu Sanniang: She is not the slightest bit annoyed with him—'only watch, don't chase' is the gesture she herself made, structurally identical to the earlier rule he set of 'only recognize the face, don't act.' That bit of fierceness is still aimed entirely at the people in the dock who set up this trap; now that official boots have appeared, the fierceness becomes even more directed: someone in the authorities is mixed up in this affair.

Liu Sanniang: She gestures to him across the rubble—the two of them each guarding one place, each carrying half a life, but this gesture is the unspoken tacit understanding between old acquaintances. The warmth is real; it is just that twelve years of old accounts are still mixed into that warmth, and once the official boots appear, another layer of cold is pressed beneath it.

Liu Sanniang: As soon as the official boots appeared, the ledger in her mind immediately turned a page: people from the authorities have gotten involved—then that clash twelve years ago, that mole case she has suspected for twelve years, did it have official-side people inside it from the very beginning? And the fact that the straw-hat guest dared come to take the black thread means the other side recognizes Tiegu Hall’s old methods. What was hanging in suspense has changed from “who will come to take the thread” to “how deep the authorities are mixed in,” and the cold sweat in her palm has thickened another layer.

Liu Sanniang: the conical-hat guest appeared, official boots entered her sight, and she still crouched among the rubble without moving or making a sound—she only gestured “watch only, do not pursue.” Steady, truly steady; it is just that beneath this steadiness lies the newly added chill of those official boots, and the two short and one long knocks on the boat in the dock, plus the likely guard at the rear ditch, remain unresolved.

Liu Sanniang: the conical-hat stranger is right in front of her, cutting away the black thread, revealing an old burn, and still wearing official boots—she does not pounce out or make a sound, but only gives a gesture meaning “watch only, do not pursue.” Over these three days, whoever loses composure first will expose themselves first; she knows that far too well. At this moment, she still proceeds according to the proper pace.

Liu Sanniang: Once the official boots appeared, the drive in her heart of "there is no way back" collided head-on with the restraint of "only watch, don't chase": if she chased after them, she might be able to seize this passerby's origins on the spot; if she did not chase, only then could she follow the line to the real principal. And the official boots expanded the doubts in the old case from "an insider" to "government involvement," changing the calculation of that twelve-year-old account by another layer. Beneath the shell, that old case, that sworn brother, that setup at Wupeng Dock—all of it is twisting together.

Liu Sanniang: The traveler in the bamboo hat had cut away the black thread; he had an old burn on his right wrist; yet on his feet were official boots—taking all three clues in at once, the ledger in her mind flipped forward several more pages: Which branch of the authorities is this man from? Is the burn on his right wrist from the fire at Qixia Ferry back then, or an old wound from somewhere else? He recognizes the black thread—is he an old member of Tiegu Hall, or someone who has thoroughly figured out Tiegu Hall’s inside story? Her pull of interest did not lessen; instead, the layer of the official boots hooked it even tighter.

Liu Sanniang: the traveler in the bamboo hat is right before her eyes, cutting away the black thread, revealing an old burn, still wearing official boots—she can only stare, unable to chase or move. The clue has come within reach but cannot be grasped, and the layer of the official boots expands the doubts around the old case even further; the account book in her heart grows heavier the more she turns it over. She feels blocked up.

Liu Sanniang: the three-day deadline has arrived, the person is already crouched in the rocky slope, and the bamboo-hat guest is right before her eyes yet can only be watched, not pursued—it is not that there is no way forward, but that every road has an ambush, and at this moment she can only guard, only wait. Urgency remains high; only the direction has shifted from “advance” to “watch,” and she watches more heavily than just now.

Liu Sanniang: She gestures to him across the rubble—the two of them each guarding one place, each carrying half a life, yet this gesture is the unspoken tacit understanding of old friends. The door opens another crack; inside the crack is a twelve-year friendship, while outside the crack, each still keeps their own cards close.

Liu Sanniang: he set the rule of "watch separately, recognize only the face and don't make a move, withdraw at once if the water duck appears"; she did as told and held the west side. Now that the bamboo-hat guest has appeared, she signals to him across the rubble, "watch only, don't pursue"—handing the right to judge back to him, so the initiative in this turn still leans half a step toward him. But the code is still hers to recognize, the appearance is still hers to determine, and the west-side watch still depends on her to make the call.

Liu Sanniang: he had set the terms—watch separately, recognize only the face, do not act—and she complied; now that she is doing better than “only watch, do not pursue,” this is boundary-keeping, not boundary-crossing. At this moment, the two of them each keep to their own boundary—he in the east, she in the west, and the traveler in the bamboo hat in the middle.

Liu Sanniang: he offers a method and sets the next step, but she still moves at her own pace—the code signal is hers to recognize, showing herself is hers to decide, and she must also make the call on guarding the western side. In this muddy water, what she agrees to is going together, not relying on him.

Liu Sanniang: the traveler in the bamboo hat cut away the black thread, had an old burn scar on his right wrist, yet wore official boots on his feet—she sized up the weight of these details at a glance: official boots mean people from the authorities have already traced their way to this line, and the fact that the other party recognized the black thread and dared to come take it shows that the route watching the rope is very familiar with Tiegu Hall’s old methods. Wupeng Dock is an old water stronghold abandoned by the Cao Gang, and the reed marshes are deep enough to swallow people; she knows that place better than anyone. As for the layer of official boots, she is more sensitive to it than anyone.

Liu Sanniang: Wupeng Dock, the canal-gang warning, that black iron token, the fire twelve years ago—all of it is pressing down on this trip. Now that official boots have appeared, the scar in her heart is pulled tighter by another degree: in that fire and clash twelve years ago, were people from the authorities involved from the very beginning? This scar is still laid open, and it has been pulled another degree tighter by this layer of official boots.

Liu Sanniang: For three days, she opened the doors as usual and let out the rumor that 'Wugeng has settled the bill and gone south,' holding the shell flawlessly. But at this moment she is not in the shop. If someone asks where the proprietress has gone, answering too deeply exposes the bottom, while answering too shallowly will not match up. And she is lying in wait on the rocky slope, keeping watch; if someone spots her, that too is a flaw. This layer of shell still has to be protected.

Liu Sanniang: There isn't the slightest thing that gives the game away; the play is still within the play—meeting at the earth temple, confirming the code phrase, the countercurrent red cord, Tiegu Hall's hidden mark in its reply, inspecting the cord and leaving a mark, two short and one long knocks on the boat, guarding the red cord to see who comes to take the black thread, splitting up to keep watch at the downwind scree slope, using a wild duck as the signal, the bamboo-hat stranger cutting the line, watching only and not giving chase—all are things old hands in this jianghu would do.

Liu Sanniang: The three-day deadline has arrived; what matters most now is meeting Lu Wenfeng at the Earth God Temple, comparing the clues each has found, and then deciding how to enter Wupeng Dock. The appearance of the conical-hat guest and the sight of the official boots are exactly what pin the conversation to this—her “only watch, don’t pursue” stance is precisely because she wants to trace this line back to the real person behind it.

Liu Sanniang: she still has to hold up the shell of "Liu Sanniang is just an innkeeper"—leaving the inn for an appointment, meeting at the Earth God Temple, guarding the rear route, and splitting up to keep watch all have to be done beneath this shell. The shell cannot break.

Liu Sanniang: The three-day deadline has arrived, and the first step of execution has settled from “guard the shop and wait for the enemy” into “meet at the Earth God Temple and decide the movements at Wupengwu,” then into “split up to watch the rope; recognize faces only, do not act.” Now that the traveler in the bamboo hat has appeared and official boots have come into view, she understands clearly in her heart that the meaning of this meal has changed another layer: from guarding the gate to entering the setup, and already arriving at the setup's doorway; the course of action is still being advanced layer by layer into finer detail.

Liu Sanniang: He offers clues, stops her, sets the next step, and even hands over the danger to her with ‘the other side won’t miss it’ and ‘there are probably also people guarding the rear ditch’; she first gives the code, first asks about what is behind him, and now further sets ‘only watch, don’t pursue’—no small talk, no approaching, keeping the topic pressed to safety and the next step. He reveals the route he came by, she reveals her movements; neither of them needs to hand over that final layer of the bottom line.

Lu Wenfeng: after checking the rope, he truthfully hands back to her the facts that “the bamboo-hat visitor cut away the black thread, had an old burn scar on his right wrist, yet wore official boots,” and further makes the gesture of “only watch, do not chase”—being willing to show her this move steadies his trust in her by another half measure. But “whether this line of hers is clean” and “why she took it without telling him last night” still remain unresolved; the impulse to trust her and the impulse to guard against her are still twisted together. It is just that in this turn, he is willing to hand the new information to her first, so the trusting impulse has a slight upper hand.

Lu Wenfeng: he returned from checking the rope and brought back ‘the bamboo-hat guest cut away the black thread,’ and further pointed out that the person ‘had an old burn on his right wrist, yet wore official boots’—the target of the investigation has expanded from jianghu people to the authorities, and this layer is heavier than in the previous turn. He immediately restrained himself with ‘only watch, don’t pursue,’ showing that his vigilance has not loosened and the retreat route is still there; it is just that another suspended matter has been added: people on the official side are also watching these three ropes.

Lu Wenfeng: He reports back intelligence and gestures “only watch, don’t chase,” which is calculating the route for both of them, not excluding her; she follows suit and splits off to infiltrate, with no antagonism either. There is not the slightest hostility; that bit of ruthlessness is still entirely elsewhere: the ghost to the north wearing Lao Wu’s name, and that “deadly shura field” at Wupeng Dock.

Lu Wenfeng: He returns what he learned from inspecting the rope truthfully into her hands, and by saying “only watch, not chase,” leaves the discretion on her side. This is the division of labor possible only between old acquaintances: he goes into the dangerous places himself, and leaves the steady ground to her. In this turn, he even hands her the layer of “official boots” to see first; it is not to refute her, but to protect her.

Lu Wenfeng: He returned from checking the rope and brought back “the traveler in a bamboo hat cut away the black thread,” further pointing out that the person “wore official boots”—the target of the investigation has expanded from jianghu figures to the authorities, adding another layer to what hangs in suspense: once he goes, whether he can come back. He then reins himself in with “only watch, don’t pursue,” showing that he can still keep his composure, but what hangs in suspense is heavier than in the previous turn.

Lu Wenfeng: He comes back after checking the rope and brings back the layer of “official boots.” What he takes in is intelligence; he does not lose composure because “people on the official side are also watching,” but instead holds the tempo steady with “only watching, not pursuing”—the rocky slope is dark, and it is unknown whether there are people outside, yet he can still stay composed.

Lu Wenfeng: He returns from checking the rope, bringing back the layer of “official boots,” yet still restrains himself with “only watch, don’t pursue,” not drawing his sword and chasing after them just because “people from the official side are watching too”—this restraint shows even more skill than in the previous turn.

Lu Wenfeng: she came as agreed, the code matched, and she even drew away the tail for him, so the part of him that trusts her gains another layer; in this turn, he even hands her the "official boots" layer first, which amounts to moving his vital point another inch closer to her. But "whether her line is clean" and "why she took it without notice last night" remain unresolved; he still leaves the discretion on her side with "only watch, do not pursue"—the force that trusts her and the force that guards against her remain twisted together, and the "official boots" layer makes these two forces tighter than in the previous turn.

He then fixed the next step with “only watch, don’t chase”: do not pursue; watch first. But “why she took it without telling anyone last night” remains unresolved.

Lu Wenfeng: after checking the rope and returning, he truthfully hands the result back to her, and further holds himself in check with 'only watch, not pursue'—this is tactical bargaining between old acquaintances, not overstepping.

Lu Wenfeng: after returning from checking the rope, he truthfully hands the result back to her, and even holds this step in place with “only watch, don’t chase”—his dependence remains low. Lu Wenfeng: he can distinguish 'the straw-hat guest cut away the black thread,' can see the 'old burn scar on the right wrist,' and can recognize that 'on the feet, however, are official boots'—this set of methods for recognizing people and routes is more precise in his hands than in the previous turn. In this turn, he further fixes the next step as 'only watch, not pursue,' showing he clearly knows whom he would alert if he chased after them.

Lu Wenfeng: He has returned from inspecting the rope, bringing back the layer of “official boots.” This scar still lies between the two of them, and closer than it was three days ago—the person who came to take the black thread was wearing official boots; in that fire-fight twelve years ago, which side were the people in officialdom on?

Lu Wenfeng: he takes the black thread, sets the division of labor and the retreat line, and in this turn further fixes the next step with “only watch, do not pursue.” This is consistent from front to back, with no self-contradiction. He still has not said aloud “where did the waist token come from, and whom do I suspect.”
Lu Wenfeng: There is no place where character was broken.

Lu Wenfeng: He returns from checking the rope and brings back the layer of “official boots,” then immediately uses “only watch, don’t pursue” to keep pushing the next step into concrete terms—the main goal of this trip is still that case, and they have already reached the final meeting before the appointment.

Lu Wenfeng: he returned from checking the rope and handed back what he learned from scouting the path, not his own bottom line; moreover, with “only watch, don’t pursue,” he seized the rhythm back into his own hands. This layer of defense has not loosened.

Lu Wenfeng: He returns from checking the rope, brings back the layer of "official boots," and then, with "only watch, not pursue," continues to push the route into the dock toward concrete ground—the purpose of his visit has not changed.

goal_tracking.trigger_summary: Three days later, at the Land Temple meeting point, Liu Sanniang matched the code with “three, one, two”, stated that she had used an empty box to draw away the tail, and recognized “three reds against the current, fellow disciples avoid the edge” and the “two short, one long” “night-crossing whistle”, while also disclosing Tiegutang Hall's hidden reply mark. After Lu Wenfeng inspected the rope and left a mark, he reported back that “the man in the bamboo hat cut away the black thread, had an old burn on his right wrist, but wore official boots”, and signaled “only watch, do not pursue”. Liu Sanniang's immediate tactical objective has been adjusted from “send Lu Wenfeng with the token along the water route to the Land Temple to scout the way, while keeping the doors open as usual to protect the shell” to “meet Lu Wenfeng at the Land Temple, compare the clues each of them has found, guard the red rope and see who comes to take the black thread, only watch and do not pursue, figure out the identity of the person setting the trap (especially the layer involving the official boots), and only then decide how to enter Wupengwu”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Arrange the food and lodging accounts for the regulars properly, while renewing old ties through reminiscing and taking the opportunity to inquire about recent movements in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Meet Lu Wenfeng at the Land Temple and compare the clues they have each uncovered; keep watch over the red cord to see who comes to retrieve the black thread, only watching and not pursuing; find out the identity of the traveler in the bamboo hat (especially the official boots), and who made the two short, one long knocks on the boat in the dock, then decide how to enter Wupeng Dock.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greeting an old regular, arranging food and lodging, quoting and settling the bill, and catching up while asking about recent circumstances.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motive: Liu Sanniang wants to figure out who is digging into the old Qixia Ferry case, why the waist token that should have sunk into the river has resurfaced, who among those who escorted the Qinglu is still alive, whether the person in the north calling himself Fifth is real or fake, which faction has followed the trail into town, and whether Lu Wenfeng's return this time is connected to any of this—now that official boots have appeared, she is even more intent on finding out which side the official authorities stood on in the fire-fight twelve years ago. But this is only an inference, and there is not yet independent evidence to substantiate it.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng states that "what I ran into wasn't a hard case, but some people digging up old accounts," and directly asks, "Has anyone recently been asking about the old survivors of the battle at Qixia Ferry?"—directly touching the old case Liu Sanniang has not mentioned to anyone for twelve years.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng pushed one layer further: he asked about "the person who escorted the Qinglu across the ferry back then," showed "the Canal Gang waist token that should have sunk into the river with the corpse," and asserted that "on the night at Qixia Ferry, perhaps someone did not die at all"—pushing the old case from "someone is asking around" to "someone did not die, and physical evidence has appeared."

In her early years, Liu Sanniang was a female escort guard for the Canal Gang. In the battle at Qixia Ferry, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an inside traitor; the back courtyard of the inn is an unmarked message relay point, and gathering rumors has always been part of her daily routine.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang received the physical evidence through action: her fingers dug into the wood seams of the counter, her fingernail nearly snapping; she gripped Lu Wenfeng’s wrist, slammed the bronze key to the Tianzi Room heavily into his palm, lowered her voice and ordered him to “go upstairs” and bolt the door, arranged a private talk at midnight, and directly pressed, “That waist token—do you have it on you?”—she proactively shifted the conversation into a locked room, breaking a twelve-year taboo.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng confirmed “it is here” and added, “the people watching it have also arrived in town”—also handing over the layer of risk that the pursuers have already reached the doorstep, expanding what Liu Sanniang needs to understand from “whose waist token it is” to “which route the pursuers come from, and whether they are already among this hall full of guests.”

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang for the first time verbally put “guarding against the old members of the grain-transport gang” on the table—“After Old Five died, there were plenty of money-grubbing ingrates in that gang; I’m more on guard against them than you are”—which was tantamount to drawing a line, in front of Lu Wenfeng, between her old fellow disciples and the old guest before her.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng used a countersign to turn the midnight appointment into an executable trust contract (“Knock three times, pause for one breath, then knock twice”; “If it isn’t that number, I won’t open the door”), then turned back to warn her, “Sanniang, you be careful too”—for the first time expressing concern for Liu Sanniang herself, expanding the risk from the layer of physical evidence to her personally.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng’s first words upon entering were “Don’t turn the lamp brighter,” after which he immediately showed his waist token and previewed that “the person in the north also left a message”—expanding the showdown from “whose waist token is it” to “who is that northern route, and what message did they leave,” while locking this conversation into a room lit by only one dim lamp.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang snatched the waist token over with one hand; the instant her fingertips touched the eagle-claw engraving, she recognized that it was Lao Wu’s token, the special black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Tiegutang”, and even remembered the chipped corner of the token (broken off back then when Lao Wu blocked a blade for her). She pressed him with “Speak!”, demanding “That damned ghost up north—what message exactly did he bring you”—for the first time, in front of physical evidence from the old case, she actively reveals her personal relationship with the deceased, pushing the interrogation toward that line from the north.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng relayed the exact words of the person from the north without missing a single character—“What sank with the blue heron was an empty account; the living account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Wharf”—and added that the person “was missing half of his right ear and called himself Old Fifth.” At the end, he asked in return, “Would outsiders know about this scar?”—turning the old case from “someone didn’t die” into “the setup back then was itself fake,” while giving a date and place, and at the same time passing the ball of identity verification to Liu Sanniang.

plot_point: Three days later, at the Earth God Temple: Lu Wenfeng arrives first and only emerges from behind the shrine after hearing footsteps, demanding the signal and asking whether the area behind is clean. Liu Sanniang knocks the pillar with “three, one, two” to match the signal, states that she used an empty case to lead the watchers to the rocky beach in the south, and reports what she learned from scouting the route—Wupeng Dock’s water surface is eerily still, without even a single waterbird; there is absolutely a trap.

Lu Wenfeng reports that three red strings tied against the current in the reeds are an old warning method of the Canal Gang; Liu Sanniang recognizes this as the old rule of Tiegu Hall, "Three reds against the current; fellow members avoid the edge," something that would never be lightly revealed unless the hall faced utter disaster, and Lao Wu back then was precisely the deputy hall master of Tiegu Hall—therefore determining that in the dock, either Lao Wu is giving a warning, or someone has thoroughly figured out Tiegu Hall's inside details and set a trap.

Liu Sanniang proposes entering the rear hold from underwater. Lu Wenfeng restrains her with “since it is a fellow sect member avoiding the edge and warning us, wouldn’t entering through the water waste the warning-giver’s intentions?” and instead suggests first checking whether the rope knots are new or old, then asks whether Tiegu Hall has any reply cipher after seeing the three reds. Liu Sanniang answers that there is—“bent reeds bound with black thread, the tip pointing to mud and sand”—and admits that just now she nearly lost her sense of proportion.

Lu Wenfeng set the division of labor: he took the black thread to test the rope and leave a mark, while Liu Sanniang would stay in the temple to watch the rear route; if he did not return within half an incense stick, she would withdraw. Liu Sanniang at first refused the order to withdraw alone, but Lu Wenfeng cornered her with “If you won’t agree to withdraw, then I won’t go”. In the end, she nodded and agreed with “half an incense stick; I won’t wait even one breath longer”, and left behind the words “your life is now entered on my account book”.

Lu Wenfeng darts out of the temple gate to inspect the ropes, while Liu Sanniang flips up onto the roof of the Earth God Temple to lie in wait, silently counting the hours, one hand on the short blade kept close to her body; in less than half an incense stick’s time, Lu Wenfeng flips back in through the rear window and reports: "The knots are new, and cinnabar sticks to the hand. As soon as the black threads were tied on, two short knocks and one long knock against a boat sounded from the fort—someone is waiting for us, and someone is also watching those three ropes."

Liu Sanniang recognizes “two short, one long” as the “night-crossing signal” of Tiegu Hall from back then, and judges that the person in the dock is either Lao Wu or someone who has set a trap after thoroughly figuring out Lao Wu's background. She immediately wants to slip through the rear ditch into the dock; Lu Wenfeng stops her with “the knocking is both a reply and a way to tell the watchers that the fish has arrived,” and instead proposes first withdrawing from the net and watching the red cord to see who comes to take the black thread.

Liu Sanniang first proposed retreating to the old locust tree behind the temple. Lu Wenfeng rejected it with, “The old locust tree is a ready-made lookout point; the other side won’t fail to notice it,” and instead set the retreat at the leeward rocky slope: split up to watch, identify newcomers only by face and do not strike, and if a second group appears, imitate a water duck once and withdraw at once. Liu Sanniang acknowledged that she had overlooked the living gate and death position, and followed his instructions to split off and move stealthily, guarding the west side.

This turn: after the time it takes to drink a cup of tea, Lu Wenfeng sees a traveler in a bamboo hat cut away a black thread; the exposed right wrist has an old burn scar, but the feet are in official boots, and from across the rubble the traveler signals to Liu Sanniang: “watch only, don’t pursue.”

Official boots mean that people from the authorities have already touched this thread, and the fact that the other party recognizes the black thread and dares to come take it means the line watching the rope is tougher than previously estimated. At this moment, in her eyes, not one place is safe.

goal_tracking.trigger_summary: Three days later, at the Land Temple meeting point, Liu Sanniang matched the code with “three, one, two”, stated that she had used an empty box to draw away the tail, and recognized “three reds against the current, fellow disciples avoid the edge” and the “two short, one long” “night-crossing whistle”, while also disclosing Tiegutang Hall's hidden reply mark. After Lu Wenfeng inspected the rope and left a mark, he reported back that “the man in the bamboo hat cut away the black thread, had an old burn on his right wrist, but wore official boots”, and signaled “only watch, do not pursue”. Liu Sanniang's immediate tactical objective has been adjusted from “send Lu Wenfeng with the token along the water route to the Land Temple to scout the way, while keeping the doors open as usual to protect the shell” to “meet Lu Wenfeng at the Land Temple, compare the clues each of them has found, guard the red rope and see who comes to take the black thread, only watch and do not pursue, figure out the identity of the person setting the trap (especially the layer involving the official boots), and only then decide how to enter Wupengwu”.
goal_tracking.long_term_goal: Arrange the food and lodging accounts for the regulars properly, while renewing old ties through reminiscing and taking the opportunity to inquire about recent movements in the jianghu.
goal_tracking.short_term_intention: Meet Lu Wenfeng at the Land Temple and compare the clues they have each uncovered; keep watch over the red cord to see who comes to retrieve the black thread, only watching and not pursuing; find out the identity of the traveler in the bamboo hat (especially the official boots), and who made the two short, one long knocks on the boat in the dock, then decide how to enter Wupeng Dock.
goal_tracking.explicit_goal: Greeting an old regular, arranging food and lodging, quoting and settling the bill, and catching up while asking about recent circumstances.
goal_tracking.underlying_goal: One possible deeper motive: Liu Sanniang wants to figure out who is digging into the old Qixia Ferry case, why the waist token that should have sunk into the river has resurfaced, who among those who escorted the Qinglu is still alive, whether the person in the north calling himself Fifth is real or fake, which faction has followed the trail into town, and whether Lu Wenfeng's return this time is connected to any of this—now that official boots have appeared, she is even more intent on finding out which side the official authorities stood on in the fire-fight twelve years ago. But this is only an inference, and there is not yet independent evidence to substantiate it.
evidence: Lu Wenfeng states that "what I ran into wasn't a hard case, but some people digging up old accounts," and directly asks, "Has anyone recently been asking about the old survivors of the battle at Qixia Ferry?"—directly touching the old case Liu Sanniang has not mentioned to anyone for twelve years.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng pushed one layer further: he asked about "the person who escorted the Qinglu across the ferry back then," showed "the Canal Gang waist token that should have sunk into the river with the corpse," and asserted that "on the night at Qixia Ferry, perhaps someone did not die at all"—pushing the old case from "someone is asking around" to "someone did not die, and physical evidence has appeared."

In her early years, Liu Sanniang was a female escort guard for the Canal Gang. In the battle at Qixia Ferry, her sworn brother died, and to this day she suspects there was an inside traitor; the back courtyard of the inn is an unmarked message relay point, and gathering rumors has always been part of her daily routine.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang received the physical evidence through action: her fingers dug into the wood seams of the counter, her fingernail nearly snapping; she gripped Lu Wenfeng’s wrist, slammed the bronze key to the Tianzi Room heavily into his palm, lowered her voice and ordered him to “go upstairs” and bolt the door, arranged a private talk at midnight, and directly pressed, “That waist token—do you have it on you?”—she proactively shifted the conversation into a locked room, breaking a twelve-year taboo.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng confirmed “it is here” and added, “the people watching it have also arrived in town”—also handing over the layer of risk that the pursuers have already reached the doorstep, expanding what Liu Sanniang needs to understand from “whose waist token it is” to “which route the pursuers come from, and whether they are already among this hall full of guests.”

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang for the first time verbally put “guarding against the old members of the grain-transport gang” on the table—“After Old Five died, there were plenty of money-grubbing ingrates in that gang; I’m more on guard against them than you are”—which was tantamount to drawing a line, in front of Lu Wenfeng, between her old fellow disciples and the old guest before her.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng used a countersign to turn the midnight appointment into an executable trust contract (“Knock three times, pause for one breath, then knock twice”; “If it isn’t that number, I won’t open the door”), then turned back to warn her, “Sanniang, you be careful too”—for the first time expressing concern for Liu Sanniang herself, expanding the risk from the layer of physical evidence to her personally.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng’s first words upon entering were “Don’t turn the lamp brighter,” after which he immediately showed his waist token and previewed that “the person in the north also left a message”—expanding the showdown from “whose waist token is it” to “who is that northern route, and what message did they leave,” while locking this conversation into a room lit by only one dim lamp.

In the previous turn, Liu Sanniang snatched the waist token over with one hand; the instant her fingertips touched the eagle-claw engraving, she recognized that it was Lao Wu’s token, the special black iron of the Canal Gang’s “Tiegutang”, and even remembered the chipped corner of the token (broken off back then when Lao Wu blocked a blade for her). She pressed him with “Speak!”, demanding “That damned ghost up north—what message exactly did he bring you”—for the first time, in front of physical evidence from the old case, she actively reveals her personal relationship with the deceased, pushing the interrogation toward that line from the north.

In the previous turn, Lu Wenfeng relayed the exact words of the person from the north without missing a single character—“What sank with the blue heron was an empty account; the living account is still there. Three days from now, bring the waist token to Wupeng Wharf”—and added that the person “was missing half of his right ear and called himself Old Fifth.” At the end, he asked in return, “Would outsiders know about this scar?”—turning the old case from “someone didn’t die” into “the setup back then was itself fake,” while giving a date and place, and at the same time passing the ball of identity verification to Liu Sanniang.

In this turn at the Earth God Temple, Liu Sanniang matches the code with “three, one, two,” states that she used an empty case to lure the watchers tailing her to the rocky shoal to the south, and recognizes “three reds against the current, same sect avoids the edge” and the “two short, one long” “night-crossing watch.” She also discloses Ironbone Hall’s reply coded mark: “broken reed tied with black thread, pointed finger in mud and sand”—for the first time, she actively tells outsiders the old rules and old codes of Ironbone Hall, breaking the old precedent of “old cases and old rules are not spoken of to others.”

After Lu Wenfeng inspected the rope and left a mark this turn, he reported back that “the straw-hat guest cut away the black thread, had an old burn scar on his right wrist, yet was wearing official boots,” and gestured “watch only, do not pursue”—for the first time, he pushes the identity clues of the person setting the trap from a jianghu gang toward the authorities, and for the first time determines the handling by gesture rather than words.
